makaleler.baslik: EAES-SAGES clinical practice guideline update: multi-society recommendations on key controversies in the management of diverticular disease.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Divertiküler Hastalık Yönetiminde Güncel EAES-SAGES Kılavuzu
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Semptomatik komplike olmayan divertiküler hastalık, komplike olmayan ve komplike divertikülit yönetimine ilişkin kanıta dayalı öneriler sunulmuştur. Sistemik derlemede 27 çalışma incelenmiş olup rifaksimin, mesalamin veya antibiyotik kullanımı gibi konularda koşullu öneriler verilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: We identified areas of controversy in the management of patients with diverticular disease to develop key questions addressing the management of symptomatic uncomplicated diverticular disease (SUDD), uncomplicated diverticulitis, and complicated diverticulitis.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review to identify randomized trials and cohort studies addressing our key questions. Informed by an updated evidence synthesis, an international, multidisciplinary panel of gastrointestinal surgeons, gastroenterologists, patient partners, and methodologists applied the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) evidence-to-decision framework during panel consensus meetings to derive recommendations for the management of patients with diverticular disease.
RESULTS: The systematic review identified 27 studies representing very low to moderate certainty evidence. The panel made the following recommendations: 1. In patients with SUDD, we suggest rifaximin or mesalamine over standard supportive care (conditional recommendation); 2. In patients with uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine antibiotics (conditional recommendation); 3. In patients with persistent symptoms following an episode of recurrent uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest elective resection over observation (conditional recommendation); 4. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine follow-up colonoscopy (conditional recommendation); 5. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of diverticulitis complicated by an abscess, we suggest elective resection over surveillance (conditional recommendation). The panel judged that a significant proportion of patients would place a high value in reducing the risk of recurrence at 1 year but also acknowledged the lack of evidence addressing prioritized outcomes including 30-day major complications, need for emergency surgery, stoma-free survival at 1 year, and quality of life at 1 year. Given that patient values and preferences may vary, clinicians are encouraged to apply patient-centered decision-making and discuss the alternatives.
CONCLUSION: This clinical practice guideline update provides evidence-informed recommendations to support patients and clinicians in the management of diverticular disease.

makaleler.baslik: Efficacy of prophylactic hemoclip placement for preventing delayed post-polypectomy bleeding in nonpedunculated colorectal lesions: updated meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis of randomized controlled trials.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Nonpedinküle Kolorektal Poliplerde Profilaktik Hemoklips Etkinliği
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 4588 hastayı içeren 10 RCT'lik bu meta-analizde, termal rezeksiyon sonrası profilaktik hemoklips uygulamasının geç kanamayı (DPPB) genel olarak azalttığı (%3,4'e karşı %6,5; RR 0,51; %95 CI 0,34-0,76; P<0,001) bildirilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Evidence regarding prophylactic hemoclip (HC) for preventing delayed post-polypectomy bleeding (DPPB) remains inconsistent. This meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA) aimed to evaluate HC after thermal resection of nonpedunculated colorectal polyps.
METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 28 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing HC with non-HC after thermal resection of nonpedunculated colorectal polyps ≥ 5 mm. The primary outcome was DPPB. Secondary outcomes included DPPB for proximal large (≥ 20 mm) nonpedunculated colorectal polyps (LNPCPs), other adverse events, and procedure time. Random-effects models, subgroup analyses, GRADE, and TSA were applied.
RESULTS: Ten RCTs involving 4,588 patients were included. HC reduced DPPB overall (3.4 vs. 6.5%; RR 0.51; 95% CI 0.34-0.76; P < 0.001; I2 = 45%; GRADE: High) and after resection of proximal LNPCPs (4.4 vs. 8.1%; RR 0.54; 95% CI 0.32-0.91; P = 0.02; I2 = 52%; GRADE: moderate). TSA supported both findings. Patients receiving antithrombotic therapy may experience greater absolute risk reduction because of higher baseline bleeding risk. HC was also associated with reduced DPPB in adenomatous lesions; however, interaction tests were nonsignificant, and subgroup findings remain exploratory. Other outcomes did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSIONS: Prophylactic HC closure reduces DPPB after thermal resection of nonpedunculated colorectal polyps ≥ 5 mm, including proximal LNPCPs. Clinical use should consider lesion characteristics, procedural factors, and individualized bleeding risk.

makaleler.baslik: Guidelines for Colonic Diverticular Disease-2026, Second Edition: Management of Diverticular Bleeding and Acute Diverticulitis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kolonik Divertiküler Hastalık ve Kanama Kılavuzu 2026
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Japon Gastroenteroloji Derneği'nin 2026 kılavuzu, divertiküler kanama ve akut divertikülit yönetimine odaklanmıştır. Risk stratifikasyonu, tanısal yaklaşımlar, endoskopik müdahaleler ve seçilmiş vakalarda primer anastomoz önerileri ele alınmıştır.
makaleler.ozet: Colonic diverticular disease is becoming increasingly common in Japan, paralleling population aging and changes in lifestyle and medication use. The predominance of right-sided diverticulosis in Asian populations, in contrast to the left-sided predominance in Western populations, influences clinical presentation and management. In Japan, diverticulitis has become a clinically important problem, and diverticular bleeding is currently the most frequent cause of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB). The Japanese Gastroenterological Association updated its clinical guidelines for diverticular bleeding and diverticulitis in 2026. Key domains including epidemiology, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and priority clinical and future research questions were addressed. Evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, and recommendations were formulated via a modified Delphi process with external review. These guidelines aim to provide Japanese and Asian evidence-based consensus that complements Western guidelines. Recommendations for acute LGIB and diverticular bleeding are as follows: risk stratification with the Shock Index and Oakland and NOBLADS scores guides triage; pre-colonoscopy contrast-enhanced computed tomography is the widely used diagnostic modality; routine colonoscopy within 24 h is not suggested for all patients; endoscopic band ligation or direct clipping is suggested post-detection of stigmata of recent hemorrhage; and early oral refeeding is suggested. Recommendations for diverticulitis are as follows: post-resolution colonoscopy is suggested to exclude colorectal cancer; outpatient treatment and withholding of antibiotics are suggested in selected uncomplicated cases; and primary anastomosis may be favored over Hartmann's procedure in selected complicated cases.

makaleler.baslik: Routine versus postoperative CRP/CT guided selective diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer: a comparative randomized controlled trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Rektum Kanseri Cerrahisi Sonrası CRP/CT Rehberliğinde Selektif İleostomi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 200 hastalı RCT'de, postoperatif CRP ve CT kılavuzluğunda selektif ileostomi stratejisi ile rutin diverjan ileostomi karşılaştırılmıştır. İleostomi oranı selektif gruba daha düşük saptanmıştır (%22,0'ye karşı %100,0, p<0,001) ve anastomoz kaçağı oranları benzer bulunmuştur (%0'a karşı %1,0).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Diverting ileostomy is routinely used to protect the anastomosis after laparoscopic low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, but it exposes most patients to stoma-related morbidity even though only a minority develop a true anastomotic leak. This trial evaluated whether a postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) and computed tomography (CT) guided selective ileostomy strategy could reduce the rate of ileostomy formation compared with routine diversion.
METHODS: In this RCT, 200 patients with stage II or III middle or lower third rectal cancer undergoing laparoscopic LAR were randomized 1:1 to a CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy group (n = 100) or a routine diverting ileostomy group (n = 100). In the CRP/CT group, serum CRP was measured daily from postoperative day 1; a threshold of 114 mg/L on day 3 or a rise greater than 15 mg/L per day triggered confirmatory contrast-enhanced CT, with ileostomy formed only if findings were suspicious for leak. The primary outcome was the stoma-free status throughout the 12-month follow-up.
RESULTS: Baseline demographic and tumor characteristics were similar between groups (all p > 0.05). Ileostomy formation was markedly lower in the CRP/CT group than the routine group (22.0% vs. 100.0%, p < 0.001). Anastomotic leak rates did not differ (0% vs. 1.0%, p = 1.000), nor did overall complication rates (31.0% vs. 32.0%, p = 0.879). Operative time (148.4 ± 14.0 vs. 166.6 ± 13.1 min, p < 0.001) and intraoperative blood loss (168.9 ± 28.2 vs. 197.3 ± 39.7 mL, p < 0.001) were significantly lower in the CRP/CT group. Stoma-related complications were far less frequent with the selective strategy (3.0% vs. 30.0%, p < 0.001). The CRP/CT group reported significantly better global health status, physical functioning, and emotional functioning scores (all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: A postoperative CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy strategy reduces the need for diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer while improving operative outcomes and quality of life; however, confirmed leakage was infrequent in both groups. This approach may serve as an alternative to routine diversion in appropriately monitored surgical units.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07722533) on July 17, 2026.

makaleler.baslik: The Use of Adhesion Barriers in Abdominopelvic Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Abdominopelvik Cerrahide Adezyon Bariyerlerinin Kullanımı
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 36 RCT ve 6729 hastayı içeren bu meta-analizde, adezyon bariyerlerinin ikinci bakı değerlendirmesinde postoperatif adezyonları anlamlı düzeyde azalttığı gösterilmiştir (21 RCT, n=2351; OR 0,37, %95 CI 0,30-0,45, p<0,00001). Ancak rutin kullanım için kanıtların henüz yetersiz olduğu vurgulanmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: The efficacy and safety of adhesion barriers in preventing postoperative adhesions remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of adhesion barriers in reducing postoperative adhesions following abdominopelvic surgery.
METHODS: CENTRAL, EMBASE and MEDLINE were searched from inception to January 15, 2025 for parallel-arm randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing adhesion barriers with controls in patients undergoing abdominopelvic surgery. Case series, case reports, reviews, animal studies, observational studies and studies involving patients with pre-existing adhesions were excluded.
RESULTS: Thirty-six RCTs involving 6729 patients were included. Adhesion barriers significantly reduced the incidence of postoperative adhesions on second-look assessment compared with controls (21 RCTs, n = 2351; OR 0.37, 95% CI 0.30-0.45, p < 0.00001; I2 = 51%; certainty of evidence: moderate). Subgroup analyses demonstrated significant reductions in postoperative adhesions in both general surgery (9 studies, n = 1162; OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.27-0.53, p < 0.00001; I2 = 27%) and obstetrics and gynecology (12 studies, n = 1189; OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.27-0.47, p < 0.00001; I2 = 62%). Pooled analysis demonstrated no significant differences between the adhesion barrier and control groups in the incidence of anastomotic leakage (9 RCTs, n = 1541), abscess formation (6 RCTs, n = 1182), wound infection (11 RCTs, n = 1084), time between initial surgery and second surgery (10 RCTs, n = 874), intraoperative blood loss (15 RCTs, n = 5327) and adhesion severity (11 RCTs, n = 756). Adhesion barriers were associated with a modest reduction in post-operative small bowel obstruction (12 RCTs, n = 4917; OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.99, p = 0.04; I2 = 38%), but were associated with a significantly longer duration of the index operation (18 RCTs, n = 5868; MD 18.66, 95% CI 11.25 to 26.06, p < 0.00001; I2 = 99%).
CONCLUSIONS: Adhesion barriers reduced adhesions at second-look assessment in a meta-analysis of pooling eight heterogeneous agent classes and procedures against an inconsistently scored surrogate outcome. Thus, evidence remains insufficient to recommend routine use or to define which patients, procedures, or risk levels warrant its use. Until adequately powered, agent-specific trials with standardized scoring and patient-centered endpoints exist, adhesion-barrier use should remain an individual clinical decision, not standard care.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD42024595564.

tez.baslik: Kolorektal malignite nedeniyle ameliyat edilen hastalarda postoperatif komplikasyonlara etki eden faktörler
tez.baslik_tr: Kolorektal Malignite Cerrahisinde Postoperatif Komplikasyon Etkenleri
tez.kisa_ozet: 804 hastanın geriye dönük incelendiği çalışmada hastaların %34,5'inde komplikasyon, %16,7'sinde majör komplikasyon geliştiği saptanmıştır. Açık cerrahi, uzamış ameliyat süresi ve düşük preoperatif albümin düzeyi genel komplikasyonlarla ilişkili bulunmuştur.
tez.ozet: Giriş ve Amaç: Postoperatif komplikasyonlar kolorektal cerrahi sonrası hastaların iyileşme süreçlerini olumsuz etkileyen önemli bir sorundur. Hastanede yatış süresinin uzaması, morbidite ve mortalite artışı gibi kısa dönem sonuçların yanı sıra adjuvan tedavinin gecikmesi ve onkolojik sonuçların kötüleşmesi gibi uzun dönem sonuçlarla da ilişkilidir. Bu nedenle komplikasyon gelişimi ile ilişkili faktörlerin belirlenmesi önem taşımaktadır. Bu çalışmada, kolorektal malignite nedeniyle küratif rezeksiyon uygulanan hastalarda postoperatif komplikasyon gelişimi ve majör komplikasyonlarla ilişkili faktörlerin belirlenmesi amaçlandı. Hastalar ve Yöntemler: İstanbul Üniversitesi İstanbul Tıp Fakültesi Genel Cerrahi Anabilim Dalı, Acil Cerrahi Servisi'nde 01.01.2014–28.02.2025 tarihleri arasında kolorektal malignite tanısıyla küratif amaçlı ameliyat edilen hastaların verileri geriye dönük olarak incelendi. Postoperatif ilk 30 gün içerisinde gelişen komplikasyonlar değerlendirildi. Komplikasyonlar Clavien-Dindo (CD) sınıflamasına göre derecelendirildi. Bulgular: Çalışmaya toplam 804 hasta dahil edildi. Hastaların ortalama yaşı 61,3±12,8 yıl olup %42,4'ünü kadınlar ve %57,6'sını erkekler oluşturuyordu. Hastaların 277'sinde (%34,5) postoperatif komplikasyon gelişirken, 134 hastada (%16,7) majör komplikasyon (CD≥3) saptandı. En sık görülen komplikasyonlar cerrahi alan enfeksiyonu (%11,7), postoperatif ileus (%7,5) ve evisserasyondu (%5,8). Çok değişkenli analizde erkek cinsiyet, açık cerrahi yaklaşım, uzamış ameliyat süresi, postoperatif yoğun bakım yatış süresinin uzunluğu, oral alıma geç başlanması ve düşük preoperatif albümin düzeyinin genel komplikasyon gelişimi ile ilişkili olduğu saptandı. Majör komplikasyon gelişimi ile ise düşük preoperatif albümin düzeyi, uzamış yoğun bakım yatışı ve serebrovasküler olay öyküsünün ilişkili olduğu bulundu. Sonuç: Kolorektal malignite nedeniyle ameliyat edilen hastalarda postoperatif komplikasyonlar önemli bir morbidite nedeni olmaya devam etmektedir. Bu bulgular, kolorektal malignite cerrahisi uygulanacak hastalarda ameliyat öncesi risk değerlendirmesinin ve özellikle nütrisyonel durumun optimize edilmesinin önemini desteklemektedir. Bu yaklaşımlar postoperatif morbiditenin azaltılmasına ve cerrahi sonuçların iyileştirilmesine katkı sağlayabilir.
tez.dergi_tam: İSTANBUL ÜNİVERSİTESİ / TIP FAKÜLTESİ / GENEL CERRAHİ ANABİLİM DALI

makaleler.baslik: IHPBA 2026 global guideline for the management of hepatocellular carcinoma in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kaynak Kısıtlı Sağlık Sistemlerinde HCC Yönetimi İçin Global Kılavuz
makaleler.kisa_ozet: IHPBA kaynak kısıtlı ortamlarda HCC tanısı ve tedavisi için global bir kılavuz yayınladı. Karaciğer rezeksiyonu korunmuş karaciğer fonksiyonlu tek veya sınırlı lezyonlarda tercih edilirken, sistemik tedavi olarak atezolizumab/bevacizumab kombinasyonu önerildi.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines for the management of patients with HCC are predominantly focused on well-resourced healthcare systems. In 2024, the IHPBA Legacy committee initiated a process to develop global resource-sensitive guidelines for the management of HCC.
METHODS: An IHPBA global guideline group produced and circulated statements on the management of HCC from diagnosis to treatment, discussed these in online webinars and generated guidelines. This document focuses on the diagnosis and management of patients with HCC in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
RESULTS: Initial diagnosis by ultrasound is supported by cross-sectional imaging. Alfa-feto protein and assessment of liver synthetic function are recommended at diagnosis. Lesion biopsy is not mandated. Liver resection is the recommended treatment of choice for single HCC in patients with preserved liver function and up to 3 lesions ≤3 cm. Radiofrequency and microwave are regarded as equivalent and can be used if resection is not available. Ethanol injection can be used if thermal ablation is not available but should be restricted to small lesions. TACE and TAE can be used for intermediate stage disease. Atezolizumab/bevacizumab combination is recommended as first line systemic therapy with sorafenib and Lenvatinib being recommended if first line is not an option. Advice for the care of the patient with advanced or terminal disease is provided.
CONCLUSIONS: This document provides resource-sensitive HCC guidelines that prioritise feasibility, maximise benefit, and reduce default reliance on best supportive care alone and are produced for the IHPBA by discussion with the global community of IHPBA.
makaleler.dergi_tam: HPB : the official journal of the International Hepato Pancreato Biliary Association

makaleler.baslik: Robotic cholecystectomy using da Vinci SP, single-site, and multiport systems: a systematic review and comparative meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Robotik Kolesistektomi Sistemlerinin Karşılaştırmalı Meta-Analizi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: da Vinci SP, Single-Site ve multiport kolesistektomi sistemlerini karşılaştıran 1.542 katılımcılı 14 çalışmalık meta-analizde, toplam operasyon ve konsol süreleri arasındaki farklar belirsiz bulundu. Cihazlar arasında belirgin bir operasyon süresi avantajı veya güvenlik üstünlüğü saptanamadı.
makaleler.ozet: Robotic platform names do not specify operative access or instrumentation. We compared da Vinci SP, Single-Site, and multiport cholecystectomy, prioritizing total operative time and planned-access completion failure. Five databases were searched in August 2026, with Scopus rerun on 6 October 2026. A registered review underwent outcome-specific, publication-based adjudication. Direct robot-to-robot mean differences were synthesized using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs). Single-incision laparoscopic cholecystectomy (SILC) comparisons were ancillary; historical indirect calculations were confined to a supplementary audit. Fourteen reports were included; nine supplied extractable direct data from analysis samples totaling 1,542 participants. For SP versus Single-Site, total operative time was very uncertain (4 studies; 580 participants; mean difference [MD] - 12.49 min; 95% CI - 36.50 to 11.53; I² = 91.0%), including one conditionally reconstructed mean. The full planned-access completion-failure composite was not estimable. Console time was secondary (4 studies; 580 participants; MD - 11.40 min; modified Hartung-Knapp 95% CI - 25.35 to 2.56; I² = 80.4%; approximate 95% prediction interval - 49.03 to 26.24). Its conventional REML-Wald CI excluded zero (- 19.43 to - 3.36), but the small-study-adjusted interval did not. Rare-event safety, long-term hernia, cost-effectiveness, and platform-specific workload evidence were insufficient. The evidence is very uncertain about differences in total operative and console time between da Vinci SP and Single-Site cholecystectomy. An overall operative-time advantage or comparative safety equivalence has not been established. The evidence does not isolate the causal effects of incision count and articulation.Review registration: PROSPERO CRD420261475321.

makaleler.baslik: Laparoscopic-guided transversus abdominis plane block with low-pressure versus standard-pressure pneumoperitoneum versus port site infiltration with standard-pressure pneumoperitoneum for postoperative pain management in laparoscopic cholecystectomy: randomized controlled trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Laparoskopik Kolesistektomide TAP Blok ve Pnömoperiton Basıncı Karşılaştırması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 180 hastada yapılan RCT'de, düşük basınçlı pnömoperiton ile laparoskopik TAP bloğun (L-TAP) erken postoperatif ağrıyı azalttığı ve omuz ağrısını düşürdüğü (%3,3'e karşı %20,0; p=0,008) görüldü. Tramadol ihtiyacı L-TAP ve S-TAP gruplarında standart gruba göre daha düşük bulundu (%8,3 ve %13,3'e karşı %41,7; p<0,001).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pain remains a significant challenge following laparoscopic cholecystectomy, influencing recovery, opioid consumption, and hospital stay. Laparoscopic-guided transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block and low-pressure pneumoperitoneum have independently demonstrated analgesic benefits. This study compared three predefined perioperative analgesic strategies: low-pressure pneumoperitoneum with laparoscopic-guided TAP block (L-TAP), standard-pressure pneumoperitoneum with TAP block (S-TAP), and standard-pressure pneumoperitoneum with port-site infiltration (S-PS).
METHODS: A prospective, open-label, three-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted at a tertiary care center (October 2022-June 2024). One hundred and eighty patients undergoing elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for cholelithiasis were randomized equally (n = 60 each). The principal outcome was postoperative pain assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) at 1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 days, and 30 days in four positions: lying, turning, coughing, and standing; standing was not assessed at 1 h. No single timepoint-position combination was designated as a standalone primary endpoint, and comparisons were interpreted as multiple outcomes. Standard analgesia comprised intravenous paracetamol 1 g QID. Rescue analgesia with intravenous tramadol 50 mg was administered when VAS ≥ 4. Secondary outcomes included shoulder-tip pain, PONV, early mobility, morphine consumption, surgical difficulty, conversion rate, and hospital stay.
RESULTS: Both TAP groups demonstrated lower VAS pain scores than S-PS at several early time points. L-TAP showed significantly lower pain scores than S-TAP during coughing and lying at 6 h (p = 0.009 for both). Shoulder-tip pain was lower in L-TAP than S-PS (3.3% vs 20.0%; p = 0.008). Rescue tramadol requirement was lower in L-TAP and S-TAP than S-PS (8.3% and 13.3% vs 41.7%; p < 0.001). Day-1 discharge rates were 96.7%, 95.0%, and 86.7%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: TAP-based strategies were associated with lower early postoperative pain and reduced rescue analgesic requirements than S-PS. L-TAP suggested additional analgesic benefit over S-TAP, although differences in local anesthetic dose, volume, and timing limit attribution to individual components.

makaleler.baslik: Resection rates after conversion therapy for initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: HCC'de konversiyon tedavisi sonrası rezeksiyon oranları
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Başlangıçta unresectable HCC hastalarında 34 çalışma ve 5137 hastayı içeren meta-analizde, konversiyon tedavisi sonrası kaba rezeksiyon oranı %20,3, modelenen havuzlanmış oran ise %25,40 (95% CI, %20,74-%30,69) olarak saptanmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: Conversion therapy may create an opportunity for liver resection in selected patients with initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but reported conversion rates use heterogeneous denominators and endpoints. We estimated actual completed hepatectomy using a verified all-treated denominator.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library/CENTRAL, Wanfang Data, and CNKI were searched through April 10, 2026. Eligible cohorts included initially or baseline unresectable HCC, an all-treated denominator, and completed liver resection events. Two authors independently assessed eligibility, extracted data, and evaluated risk of bias. Random-effects logit proportion meta-analysis, Hartung-Knapp sensitivity, prediction intervals, leave-one-out analyses, treatment-strategy subgroups, publication-year meta-regression, and small-study-effect diagnostics were undertaken. PROSPERO: CRD420261360108.
RESULTS: Thirty-seven reports represented 36 unique studies; 34 studies involving 5,137 patients and 1,042 completed hepatectomies entered the quantitative synthesis. The crude aggregate resection rate was 20.3% (1,042/5,137), whereas the random-effects modeled pooled rate was 25.40% (95% CI, 20.74%-30.69%; I2=91.5%; tau2=0.5132). The Hartung-Knapp 95% CI was 20.12%-31.51%, and the prediction interval was 7.16%-60.04%. Leave-one-out estimates ranged from 24.52% to 26.64%. Treatment-strategy differences were not statistically significant (Qm=5.17, df=2, P = 0.075). Publication-year meta-regression did not show a clear linear association (OR per decade 1.19, 95% CI 0.77-1.83; P = 0.440), and Egger's test did not indicate significant funnel asymmetry (P = 0.381).
CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one-quarter of patients initiating conversion therapy underwent actual hepatectomy, but the crude and modeled estimates differ because substantial heterogeneity changes random-effects study weighting. The pooled estimate is a cross-study, cross-era benchmark for multidisciplinary decision-making rather than a universal patient-level probability or a treatment-specific efficacy estimate.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261360108.

makaleler.baslik: External oblique intercostal plane block improves early postoperative analgesia after open liver surgery: A randomized, double-blind, controlled trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Açık karaciğer cerrahisinde EOI blok analjezisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Açık karaciğer cerrahisi geçiren 74 hastanın alındığı çift kör RCT'de, EOI blok grubunda postoperatif 3. saatteki dinlenme NRS ağrı skoru anlamlı derecede düşük bulunmuş ve hastanede kalış süresi daha kısa saptanmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: The external oblique intercostal (EOI) plane block is a fascial plane block that targets the unilateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves, and spares the sympathetic trunk. We hypothesized that the ultrasound-guided EOI plane block might provide superior analgesia compared to systemic analgesia alone for patients after open liver surgery.
METHODS: In this double-blind, randomized controlled trial, 74 patients scheduled for open liver surgery were assigned to receive either EOI plane block with 30 mL of 0.375% ropivacaine (n = 37) or no EOI plane block (n = 37). All patients received postoperative standard patient-controlled intravenous analgesia. Primary outcome was the resting numerical rating scale (NRS) pain score at 3 h postoperatively. The key secondary outcomes included opioid consumption, and the total number of analgesia interventions at 3 h, 6 h, 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h postoperatively; opioid-related side effects and block-related complications; postoperative functional recovery outcomes; total ropivacaine plasma concentrations at 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, and 180 min post-block.
RESULTS: The primary outcome, the resting NRS pain score at 3 h postoperatively, was significantly lower in the block group than in the control group. The block group showed a shorter length of hospital stay. There were no significant differences in cumulative opioid consumption, frequency of analgesia, or opioid-related side effects. No block-related complications were observed, and total ropivacaine plasma concentrations remained below the toxicity threshold.
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided EOI plane block reduces early postoperative pain. This technique should be regarded as a safe and effective component within a comprehensive postoperative multimodal analgesia regimen.

tez.baslik: Preoperatif serum pentraxin-3 değerinin kolesistektomi zorluk derecesini öngörmekteki yeri
tez.kisa_ozet: Elektif laparoskopik kolesistektomi planlanan 80 hastanın incelendiği prospektif tez çalışmasında, preoperatif serum PTX-3 düzeyinin zor kolesistektomi için bağımsız bir öngörücü olduğu saptanmıştır (aOR=21,26; p<0,001).
tez.ozet: Amaç: Bu çalışma semptomatik kolelitiyazis nedeni ile elektif kolesistektomi planlanan hastalarda preoperatif dönemde ölçülen pentraxin-3 (PTX-3) seviyesinin kolesistektominin zorluk derecesini öngörmekteki tanısal performansını değerlendirmeyi amaçlamaktadır. Gereç ve Yöntem: SBÜ Bursa Yüksek İhtisas Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi Genel Cerrahi Kliniğinde Ağustos 2025 – Ocak 2026 tarihleri arasında elektif laparoskopik kolesistektomi planlanan, semptomatik kolelitiyazis tanılı 80 hasta prospektif olarak çalışmaya dahil edildi. PTX-3 seviyesini etkileyebilecek ek hastalığı bulunan, aktif akut kolesistit ya da malignite tanısı olan hastalar dışlandı. Tüm hastaların preoperatif dönemde demografik, klinik, görüntüleme ve biyokimyasal verileri kayıt altına alındı; operasyon sabahı serum PTX-3 ve CRP, ALP, GGT düzeyleri ölçüldü. İntraoperatif zorluk Nassar Zorluk Skalası ile belirlendi; toplam operasyon süresi ve Calot üçgeni diseksiyon süresi ayrıca kaydedildi. Hastalar Nassar Grade 1-2 (zor olmayan vaka) ve Grade 3-4 (zor vaka) olmak üzere iki gruba ayrıldı; PTX-3 düzeyinin tanısal performansı ROC analizi ile değerlendirildi, bağımsız öngörücüler ikili lojistik regresyon ile belirlendi. Bulgular: Çalışmaya dahil edilen 80 hastanın 26'sı (%32,5) Nassar Grade 3-4 zor vaka grubunda yer aldı. Preoperatif serum PTX-3 düzeyi zor vaka grubunda anlamlı şekilde yüksek bulundu (medyan 1335,2 vs 948,8 pg/mL; p 1033,81 pg/mL olarak belirlendi; bu değerde AUC 0,841 (%95 GA: 0,742-0,913), duyarlılık %84,62, özgüllük %79,63, pozitif prediktif değer %66,70 ve negatif prediktif değer %91,50 olarak hesaplandı. Çok değişkenli lojistik regresyon analizinde PTX-3 >1033,81 pg/mL olması (aOR=21,26; %95 GA: 5,29-85,47; p<0,001) zor kolesistektomi için bağımsız öngörücü olarak saptandı. PTX-3 düzeyi ile toplam operasyon süresi (rs=0,448; p<0,001) ve Calot diseksiyon süresi (rs=0,369; p=0,001) arasında pozitif yönlü orta düzeyde korelasyon bulundu. Sonuç: Çalışmamız elektif laparoskopik kolesistektomi planlanan semptomatik kolelitiyazis hastalarında preoperatif serum PTX-3 düzeyinin zor cerrahi öngörüsünde güçlü bir bağımsız öngörücü ve klinik kullanıma aday bir biyobelirteç olduğunu ortaya koymuştur. CRP'nin bu çalışmadaki prediktif performansının sınırlı olduğu ve bu öngörü görevi için PTX-3'ün potansiyel bir biyobelirteç olduğu gösterilmiş; ayrıca PTX-3 düzeyinin operasyon süresi tahmininde de katkı sağlayabileceği saptanmıştır. PTX-3 ölçümü, deneyimli cerrahın görevlendirilmesi ve perioperatif planlamanın bireyselleştirilmesi açısından klinik karar verme sürecine değerli bir katkı sunabilir.

makaleler.baslik: Preoperative Injection of Botulinum Toxin Into the Sphincter of Oddi Does Not Prevent Pancreatic Fistula After Distal Pancreatectomy: The Randomized Controlled PREBOTPilot Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Distal Pankreatektomi Sonrası Botulinum Toksin Enjeksiyonu Pankreatik Fistülü Önlemiyor
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 50 hastanın alındığı monokentli RCT'de, cerrahi öncesi Sphincter of Oddi'ye botulinum toksin enjeksiyonunun distal pancreatectomy sonrası klinik olarak anlamlı POPF oranını azaltmadığı gösterildi (intervention grubunda %28,6, kontrol grubunda %15; p=0.294).
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether preoperative injection of botulinum toxin (BTX) into the sphincter of Oddi (SO) is a safe and feasible strategy to prevent postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) after distal pancreatectomy (DP).
SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: POPF remains a common and potentially serious complication following DP, affecting up to 30% of patients. Pharmacologically induced sphincter relaxation by endoscopic injection of BTX into the SO has been described as a new approach to prevent POPF after DP by improved drainage of pancreatic fluid towards the duodenum.
METHODS: Patients scheduled for elective primary distal pancreatectomy (DP), irrespective of the underlying disease, were included in this monocenter, randomized controlled, open-label, phase-II trial with 2 parallel arms. Patients randomly assigned to the intervention group received an endoscopic injection of BTX (100 units) into the SO 3-10 days before surgery. Patients in the control group did not undergo any preoperative intervention. The combined primary endpoint was defined as the occurrence of clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF grades B/C) and/or death due to any cause within 30 days following DP.
RESULTS: From March 2020 to August 2023, 50 patients were included in the trial. Subsequent to the analysis of the primary endpoint, which revealed no tendency of a beneficial effect on the rate of POPF after DP following BTX injection, even with the most favorable outcome upon further inclusion of the remaining 10 patients planned for recruitment, the recruitment was prematurely terminated. All 26 patients in the intervention group underwent successful SO BTX injection within a median of 6 (IQR of 5-8) days before surgery. DP was performed in 41 patients (82%). Postinterventional pancreatitis was not detected. Within 30 days, POPF grade B/C occurred in 6 patients in the intervention and 3 patients in the control group (28.6% vs. 15%, P=0.294). One patient in the intervention group died during the trial due to POPF-induced postpancreatectomy hemorrhage (PPH).
CONCLUSION: Preoperative injection of BTX into the SO did not reduce clinically relevant POPF or 30-day mortality following DP, and the trial was prematurely terminated for futility. Although the intervention was safe and feasible, these findings do not support its use for the prevention of POPF after DP.

makaleler.baslik: Predictive Factors for Occult Metastases in Clinically M0 Pancreatic Cancer: A Prospective Multicenter Analysis of Staging Laparoscopy.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Klinik M0 Pankreas Kanserinde Okkült Metastazları Öngören Faktörler
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 199 hastanın alındığı prospektif çok merkezli çalışmada staging laparoscopy (SL) ile genel metastaz oranı %25,1 saptandı. Neoadjuvan tedavi almayan 152 hastada, BR/URLA durumu (OR 3,261; %95 CI 1,185-9,483, p=0,022) ve gövde/kuyruk yerleşimi (OR 2,653; %95 CI 1,037-7,214, p=0,042) okkült metastaz için bağımsız risk faktörleri olarak bulundu.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Staging laparoscopy (SL) is a minimally invasive approach for detecting occult metastases in patients with pancreatic cancer (PC) without signs of metastasis on imaging. This study aimed to identify the predictive factors for imaging-negative occult metastases.
METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 199 patients with histologically confirmed PC from three institutions between August 2021 and April 2023. All patients were scheduled for a treatment plan that included SL.
RESULTS: The overall metastasis rate as detected using SL was 25.1%, which varied from 20.6% in patients with resectable PC (R-PC) to 33.8% in those with borderline resectable or locally advanced unresectable PC (BR/URLA-PC). In 152 patients who did not receive neoadjuvant therapy, BR/URLA status (odds ratio 3.261; 95% confidence interval 1.185-9.483, p = 0.022) and pancreatic body/tail lesions (odds ratio 2.653; 95% confidence interval 1.037-7.214, p = 0.042) were independent risk factors for occult metastatic lesions (M1). Among the 107 patients with R-PC, M1 disease was significantly associated with pancreatic body/tail lesions, tumor size, and elevated levels of tumor markers. In particular, elevated carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels were consistent across all patients with M1 pancreatic head cancer. In contrast, no statistical differences were observed for any of these factors in the 45 patients with BR/URLA-PC.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support the importance of SL in patients with BR/UR PC. For R-PC, patients with pancreatic head lesions and normal tumor marker values may represent a very low-risk subgroup where selective omission of SL can be considered in resource-constrained settings.

makaleler.baslik: Clinical Efficacy of Tislelizumab Plus Gemcitabine-Nab-Paclitaxel for Borderline Resectable Pancreatic Cancer and Chemoresistance Analysis: A Prospective Pilot Study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Borderline Resekte Pankreas Kanserinde Neoadjuvan Tislelizumab Tedavisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 30 hastanın alındığı prospektif pilot çalışmada, neoadjuvan tislelizumab plus gemcitabine ve nab-paclitaxel ile R0 rezeksiyon hızı %80,0 (24/30) olarak bildirildi. 12 aylık OS %87,5 (%95 CI 64,3-95,8%), medyan RFS ise 28 ay (%95 CI 16,9-39,1) bulundu.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant therapy can improve the survival outcomes of patients with borderline resectable pancreatic cancer (BRPC). However, standard neoadjuvant regimens remain lacking. This study evaluated the clinical feasibility of tislelizumab plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel in the neoadjuvant setting for BRPC.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, patients with BRPC preoperatively received three cycles of tislelizumab plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel, and continued postoperatively. The primary endpoints were R0 resection rate and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). Exploratory objectives were resistance to this regimen.
RESULTS: Of 30 enrolled patients, 80.0% (24/30) completed neoadjuvant therapy and underwent surgical resection. R0 resection was achieved in 80.0% (24/30) of the patients and in 100.00% (24/24) of those resected. The 12-month OS and RFS rates were 87.5% (95% CI 64.3-95.8%) and 82.8% (95% CI 60-95.8%), respectively, with median RFS of 28 months (95% CI 16.9-39.1). Most TRAEs were grade I-II, with no serious events. Quantitative proteomics combined with machine learning identified NT5DC2, FAM3D, CXCL5, and TMT1B as candidate biomarkers of resistance to this neoadjuvant regimen. In paired pre- and postoperative tissues from treatment-sensitive patients, CD8+ T-cell infiltration tended to increase and CD163+ M2-like macrophages were significantly upregulated after surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Neoadjuvant tislelizumab plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel is promising for improving the resection rate in BRPC, with a favorable safety profile. NT5DC2, FAM3D, CXCL5, and TMT1B may serve as candidate biomarkers of preoperative drug resistance, and tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) analysis further reveals immune microenvironment remodeling in postoperative tumors from treatment-sensitive patients. These findings warrant validation in larger-scale studies. Trial Registration Chinese Clinical Trial registry (ChiCTR2200063680).

makaleler.baslik: Comparison of endoscopic and radiologic drainage for symptomatic postoperative pancreatic fistula-associated collections after distal pancreatectomy.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Distal Pankreatektomi Sonrası Semptomatik Koleksiyonlar için Drenaj Yöntemlerinin Karşılaştırılması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 607 hastanın incelendiği retrospektif çalışmada, POPF ile ilişkili semptomatik koleksiyonlar için birinci basamak endoskopik drenaj, radyolojik drenaja kıyasla toplam hastane kalış süresini kısma ile ilişkili bulundu (19'a karşı 31 gün; p=0,023).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: After distal pancreatectomy (DP), symptomatic postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF)-associated collections are common and lead to readmissions. The choice of drainage modality remains debated. This study compared endoscopic and radiologic drainage as first-line treatment.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included patients undergoing DP with or without splenectomy from 2012 to 2024. Patients who underwent DP with a concomitant digestive or vascular procedure or pancreatic anastomosis were excluded. The primary outcome was total hospital stay, defined as the sum of the index hospitalization and readmissions.
RESULTS: Among 607 patients, 124 (20.4%) had POPF, including 94 (15.5%) with a symptomatic collection. Of these, 25 underwent endoscopic drainage (lumen-apposing metal stent, n = 19; double-pigtail stent, n = 6), 12 underwent radiologic drainage, and 57 received another treatment (medical treatment alone, n = 35; drain tract recanalization, n = 15; surgical reoperation, n = 4; endoscopic sphincterotomy, n = 3). The endoscopic and radiologic drainage groups were comparable, except for collection location adjacent to the pancreatic transection margin (endoscopic: 92% vs radiologic: 50%; p = 0.008). Total hospital stay within 90 days was shorter after endoscopic drainage (19 vs 31 days; p = 0.023), with no deaths within 90 days. The clinical success rate was higher after endoscopic drainage (76% vs 50%; p = 0.15), whereas drainage dysfunction was more frequent after radiologic drainage (17% vs 4%; p = 0.2). Four severe complications occurred: three after endoscopic drainage using a LAMS, including two hemorrhagic complications, and one after radiologic drainage. In univariable analysis, collection location adjacent to the pancreatic transection margin and endoscopic drainage were associated with shorter total hospital stay within 90 days (β = - 17 days; 95% CI - 29 to - 4.2; p = 0.010 and β = - 13 days; 95% CI - 24 to - 1.6; p = 0.026, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: After DP, first-line endoscopic drainage of symptomatic POPF-associated collections was associated with a shorter total hospital stay and a trend toward a higher clinical success rate but may carry a risk of bleeding.

makaleler.baslik: Optimizing drain management following distal pancreatectomy: fewer drains and earlier removal guided by drain fluid amylase and C-reactive protein levels.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Distal Pankreatektomi Sonrasında Dren Yönetiminin Amilaz ve CRP ile Optimizasyonu
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 258 hastanın retrospektif analizinde CR-POPF oranı %28,3 bulundu. Multivaryabl analize göre DFA3 ≥ 1000 U/L (OR 8,21; P<0,001) ve CRP3 ≥ 12 mg/dL (OR 3,37; P=0,004) CR-POPF için bağımsız öngörücüler olarak saptandı.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Appropriate postoperative drain management, including early drain removal, is crucial following distal pancreatectomy (DP). This study aimed to investigate reliable criteria for early drain removal and the optimal drain placement site.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing DP from 2014 to 2024, with drains placed at the pancreatic stump and/or the left subphrenic space. Short-term outcomes were compared according to clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula (CR-POPF) occurrence, and the risk factors were identified.
RESULTS: Among 258 patients who underwent DP, 85.7% (n = 221) used two drains. CR-POPF developed in 28.3% (n = 73). The CR-POPF group demonstrated higher body mass index, less frequent minimally invasive surgery, greater blood loss, and more transfusions than the no CR-POPF group. The CR-POPF group exhibited significantly higher drain fluid amylase and C-reactive protein levels on postoperative days (POD) 1 and 3 (DFA1/3 and CRP1/3). Multivariable analysis identified DFA3 ≥ 1,000 U/L (odds ratio [OR] 8.21; P < 0.001), CRP3 ≥ 12 mg/dL (OR 3.37; P = 0.004), laparotomy (OR 3.26; P = 0.007), age (OR 1.04; P = 0.049), and operative time (OR 1.01; P = 0.006) as independent predictors for CR-POPF. The left subphrenic drain showed lower DFA1/3 values and a lesser association with CR-POPF than the pancreatic stump drain.
CONCLUSION: DFA3 and CRP3 may function as practical indicators for early drain removal. Left subphrenic drain may be considered for omission when an effective drain is placed at the pancreatic stump.

tez.baslik: Pankreatoduedonektomi sonrası pankreatik fistül gelişiminin preoperatif bilgisayarlı tomografi bulgularıyla öngörülmesi: Retrospektif bir analiz
tez.baslik_tr: Whipple Prosedürü Sonrası Pankreatik Fistülün BT Bulgularıyla Öngörülmesi
tez.kisa_ozet: Whipple prosedürü uygulanan 175 hastanın incelendiği retrospektif çalışmada, hastaların %24'ünde CR-POPF geliştiği saptanmıştır. Çok değişkenli analizde Wirsung kanalı çapı (OR=0,65; p=0,022) ve VYA/İKİ oranı (OR=1,15; p=0,023) pankreatik fistül gelişiminde bağımsız risk faktörleri olarak belirlenmiştir.
tez.ozet: Amaç: Whipple prosedürü uygulanan hastalarda pankreatikojejunostomi kaçakları çok önemli bir sorundur ve preoperatif dönemde riskin belirlenmesi büyük önem taşımaktadır. Biz bu çalışmamızda periampuller tümör nedeni ile kliniğimizde whipple prosedürü uygulanan hastalarda preoperatif bilgisayarlı tomografi görüntülerini retrospektif olarak inceleyerek postoperatif pankreatik fistüller ile arasında bağlantı olup olmadığını araştırmayı amaçladık. Gereç ve Yöntem: Ocak 2019 ile Aralık 2025 tarihleri arasında Ankara Bilkent Şehir Hastanesi'nde whipple prosedürü uygulanan 175 hasta çalışmaya dahil edilmiştir. Çalışma retrospektif olarak tasarlanmıştır. Preoperatif dönemdeki bilgisayarlı tomografi görüntüleri radyoloji hekimleri tarafından incelenmiş ve ölçümleri yapılmıştır. Klinik veriler hastane kayıt sistemi ve klinik arşivinden alınmıştır Bulgular: Çalışmaya dahil edilen 175 hastanın 42'sinde (%24) klinik açıdan anlamlı postoperatif pankreatik fistül (CR-POPF) geliştiği saptanmıştır. Bunların 26'sı (%61,9) Grade B, 16'sı (%38,1) Grade C fistül olarak değerlendirilmiştir. CR-POPF gelişen grupta ortalama Wirsung kanalı çapı (3,62±1,77 mm), gelişmeyen gruba (5,67±2,67 mm) göre istatistiksel olarak anlamlı düzeyde düşük bulunmuştur (p<0,001). ROC analizi sonucunda CR-POPF öngörüsünde Wirsung çapı için 4,5 mm kesim değeri (AUC: 0,75; %78,6 sensitivite, %59,4 spesifisite) belirlenmiştir. B/W oranı (p<0,001), Visseral Yağ Doku (VYA) (p=0,007), Subkutan Yağ Doku (SYA) (p=0,041) ve VYA/İKİ oranı (p=0,011) CR-POPF gelişimi üzerinde anlamlı etkili bulunmuştur. Çok değişkenli analiz sonucunda Wirsung kanalı çapı (OR=0,65; p=0,022) ve VYA/İKİ oranı (OR=1,15; p=0,023) bağımsız risk faktörleri olarak saptanmıştır. Yaş, cinsiyet, Diabetes Mellitus varlığı ve pankreas başı HU yoğunluğu ile CR-POPF gelişimi arasında anlamlı bir ilişki saptanmamıştır ix Sonuç: Preoperatif bilgisayarlı tomografi (BT) üzerinden yapılan morfometrik ölçümler, Whipple prosedürü sonrası CR-POPF gelişimini öngörmede güvenilir sonuçlar sunmaktadır. Özellikle Wirsung kanalı çapının 4,5 mm'nin altında olması ve VYA/İKİ oranının yüksekliği (sarkopenik obezite göstergesi), fistül gelişimi için en güçlü bağımsız risk faktörleridir. Bu parametrelerin operasyon öncesi değerlendirilmesi, yüksek riskli hasta grubunun belirlenmesine ve cerrahi stratejilerin (anastomoz tekniği seçimi, stent kullanımı vb.) kişiye özel planlanmasına olanak sağlayarak postoperatif morbiditeyi azaltabilir.

makaleler.baslik: Uniportal versus Multiportal Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery for Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy in Esophageal Cancer: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Minimal İnvaziv Özofajektomide Uniportal ve Multiportal VATS Karşılaştırması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 9 çalışmanın dahil olduğu meta-analizde, uVATS birinci gün postoperatif ağrıyı (MD -2,10; %95 CI -3,63 ila -0,57), postoperatif pnömoniyi (OR 0,41; %95 CI 0,22-0,76) ve hastanede kalış süresini (MD -2,13 gün; %95 CI -3,64 ila -0,63) anlamlı düzeyde azaltmıştır. Anastomoz kaçağı ve genel komplikasyon oranlarında ise iki yaklaşım arasında anlamlı fark gözlenmemiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive esophagectomy has become the preferred surgical approach for esophageal cancer, with uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS) emerging as a potential refinement over conventional multiportal VATS (mVATS). However, comparative evidence remains limited to small single-centre studies. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively evaluate perioperative and safety outcomes of uVATS versus mVATS in patients undergoing minimally invasive esophagectomy.
METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and CNKI from inception through April 2026. Studies directly comparing uVATS with mVATS in adults undergoing minimally invasive esophagectomy were eligible. Binary outcomes were pooled as odds ratios and continuous outcomes as mean differences under REML random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using I² statistics. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework.
RESULTS: Nine studies comparing uVATS and mVATS were included. uVATS was associated with significantly lower postoperative pain on day one (MD - 2.10, 95% CI - 3.63 to - 0.57; I² = 99.3%), reduced postoperative pneumonia (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22-0.76; I² = 43.5%), and shorter length of hospital stay (MD - 2.13 days, 95% CI - 3.64 to - 0.63; I² = 96.8%). No significant differences were observed between approaches for anastomotic leakage (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.61-2.09), overall complications (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.47-1.32), recurrent laryngeal nerve injury (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.43-1.85), perioperative mortality (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.16-1.81), intraoperative blood loss, or total operative time.
CONCLUSION: UVATS esophagectomy appears to be a feasible and safe alternative to mVATS, with potential advantages in postoperative pain, pulmonary morbidity, and hospital stay while maintaining comparable perioperative safety. The evidence base remains limited by high heterogeneity and predominance of observational studies. Multicenter randomized trials with standardized protocols and long-term oncologic follow-up are needed to consolidate these findings.

makaleler.baslik: Aerosolized prostaglandin E1 improves oxygenation during one-lung ventilation: A dose-finding randomized controlled trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Aerosol Prostaglandin E1 Tek Akciğer Ventilasyonunda Oksijenasyonu Artırır
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 160 hastayla yapılan RCT'de, tek akciğer ventilasyonu sırasında nebulize Prostaglandin E1 oksijenasyonu artırmış ve pulmoner şantı azaltmıştır. En yüksek etkinlik 0,3 mikrogram/kg dozunda görülmüştür.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the effects of varying doses of aerosolized Prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) on oxygenation and intrapulmonary shunt fraction (Qs/Qt) during One-Lung Ventilation (OLV) under 60% Fraction of Inspired Oxygen (FiO2). Secondary objectives included evaluating the impact on intraoperative hypoxemia, postoperative Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS), and Postoperative Pulmonary Complications (PPCs).
DESIGN: A prospective, single center, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial.
SETTING: The study was conducted at a single academic medical center.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 160 patients aged 65‒84 years, with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status II or III and Body Mass Index (BMI) < 30 kg/m2, undergoing elective esophageal cancer surgery were enrolled. Patients with certain comorbidities, respiratory diseases, or contraindications to PGE1 were excluded.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned to one of four groups: Group L ‒ Received 0.1 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group M ‒ Received 0.2 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group H ‒ Received 0.3 μg/kg PGE1 nebulization; Group C (control) ‒ Received normal saline nebulization. Nebulization was performed for 10-minutes via a modified breathing circuit into the ventilated lung before initiating OLV.
MEASUREMENTS: Arterial blood gas parameters (arterial partial pressure of oxygen, PaO2; arterial oxygen saturation, SaO2; arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide, PaCO2), hemodynamic variables (Mean Arterial Pressure [MAP]; Heart Rate [HR]), respiratory mechanics (Peak airway pressure [Ppeak]; dynamic lung compliance [Cdyn]), PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and Qs/Qt were recorded at multiple time points during OLV. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia and hypotension, PPCs within 7-days, and CPIS on postoperative day-2 were also assessed.
MAIN RESULTS: All PGE1 groups showed significantly improved PaO2, SaO2, and PaO2/FiO2 ratio, and reduced Qs/Qt during the first 30-minutes of OLV compared to the control group. The High-dose group (H) demonstrated the greatest improvement in oxygenation. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [Group L: 0/40 (0%), Group M: 0/40 (0%), Group H: 0/40 (0%), Group C: 3/40 (7.5%)] and hypotension did not differ significantly among groups; however, the hypoxemia finding was exploratory as the study was not powered for this endpoint. No significant differences were observed in PPCs incidence among groups, but group H was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 compared to group C. Hemodynamic changes were transient and clinically manageable.
CONCLUSIONS: Nebulized PGE1 at doses of 0.1-0.3 μg/kg improves oxygenation and reduces Qs/Qt during OLV under 60% oxygen, with the 0.3 μg/kg dose being most effective. It did not significantly reduce the incidence of PPCs within 7-days. The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was lower in the PGE1 groups (0/120) compared with the control group (3/40), but this was an exploratory finding as the study was not powered for this endpoint. The higher dose (0.3 μg/kg) was associated with a lower CPIS on postoperative day-2 (3.3 vs. 4.1), but CPIS is a surrogate marker, and this finding should be interpreted as exploratory. The clinical significance of this small difference is uncertain, as changes of this magnitude are below the typically recognized thresholds for meaningful clinical improvement. Hemodynamic monitoring is recommended when using higher doses of PGE1.

makaleler.baslik: Development and validation of an explainable model for predicting lymph node metastasis in early gastric cancer: a multicenter retrospective study with external and prospective validation.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Erken Mide Kanserinde Lenf Nodu Metastazı için Açıklanabilir Model
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 3412 hastanın eğitim kohortunda geliştirilen XGBoost modeli, dış ve prospektif validasyonlarda lenf nodu metastazını öngörmede yüksek AUC değerleri (0,8583 ve 0,8766) göstermiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Accurate preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is essential for treatment selection in early gastric cancer (EGC), particularly when considering endoscopic submucosal dissection. Existing approaches show limited sensitivity for metastatic disease and frequently lack external or prospective validation. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning model for individualized preoperative prediction of LNM in EGC.
METHODS: In this multicenter study, four cohorts from three tertiary centers were included. Patients with pathologically confirmed EGC who underwent gastrectomy with lymph node dissection were retrospectively enrolled for training and external validation. A temporally independent cohort (September 2023-December 2024) was prospectively enrolled for validation. A preoperative pathology validation cohort (January 2025-January 2026) was also analyzed. Clinicopathological variables were selected using LASSO regression. SMOTE was applied to address class imbalance. Six machine-learning algorithms were compared. Model performance was assessed using AUC and PR-AUC, and interpretability was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations. A web-based calculator was developed.
RESULTS: Among 3412 patients in the training cohort, 467 (13.7%) had LNM. XGBoost achieved the best discrimination (training AUC = 0.9289) and maintained robust performance in the external (AUC = 0.8583; PR-AUC = 0.6079) and prospective validation cohorts (AUC = 0.8766; PR-AUC = 0.5137). In the preoperative pathology validation cohort, the model achieved an AUC of 0.8653 and a PR-AUC of 0.6050. Key predictors included lymphovascular/neural invasion, invasion depth, tumor location, differentiation, and tumor size.
CONCLUSIONS: This externally and prospectively validated, interpretable machine-learning model provides transparent individualized risk estimates and may support personalized decision-making between endoscopic and surgical management in EGC.

makaleler.baslik: Nivolumab-Ipilimumab for Localized Microsatellite Instability-High Gastric/Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma: The Phase 2 NEONIPIGA Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Lokalize MSI-High Mide ve GEJ Adenokarsinomunda Nivolumab-İpilimumab
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 32 hastanın alındığı evre 2 NEONIPIGA çalışmasında, neoadjuvan nivolumab ve ipilimumab ile tedavi edilen ve cerrahiye giden hastalarda 4 yıllık OS %84,1, EFS ise %83,5 olarak bildirilmiştir. Cerrahi specimenlerde pCR oranı %59 (17/29) olarak saptanmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
IMPORTANCE: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab in localized deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma was evaluated in the NEONIPIGA study. The primary end point of pathological complete response (pCR) was previously reported.
OBJECTIVE: To report long-term follow-up results and secondary end points, including event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS), of the NEONIPIGA study.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The NEONIPIGA study is a French, multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial that included patients with histologically proven cT2-T4NXM0 deficient mismatch repair/microsatellite instability-high GEJ adenocarcinoma who were eligible for surgery. Patients were enrolled between October 23, 2019, and June 4, 2021, and the database was locked on November 13, 2025.
INTERVENTION: Neoadjuvant nivolumab, 240 mg, every 2 weeks for 6 cycles plus ipilimumab, 1 mg/kg, every 6 weeks for 2 cycles, followed by surgery 5 weeks after the last nivolumab dose, and adjuvant nivolumab, 480 mg, every 4 weeks for 9 cycles.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: EFS and OS.
RESULTS: A total of 32 patients (median [range] age, 65 [40-80] years; 8 [28%] female and 21 [72%] were male) were included: 16 (50%) with gastric cancer and 16 (50%) with GEJ cancer. Three patients did not undergo surgery (1 with metastatic disease and 2 who refused). Twenty-seven patients (84%) completed neoadjuvant therapy and 14 (44%) received all treatment as planned. Neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy-related grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 6 (19%) and 4 patients (17%), respectively. Median follow-up was 48.3 months (95% CI, 44.8-52.0 months). Among the 32 patients in the intention-to-treat population, 4-year OS was 84.1% (95% CI, 65.8%-93.0%). In the 31 patients eligible for surgery, 4-year EFS was 83.5% (95% CI, 64.8%-92.8%). One patient relapsed with cerebral metastases. Six deaths occurred: 2 related to gastric cancer or treatment (1 patient had postoperative complications and 1 cerebral metastases) and 4 unrelated. All patients who did not undergo surgery achieved a clinical complete response after immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. One patient subsequently died of causes unrelated to their cancer. Overall, 17 of 29 patients (59%) achieved pCR on surgical specimen. Safety was previously reported, and no additional late toxic effects were observed.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial, the immunotherapy regimen evaluated was associated with sustained long-term survival, but no clear evidence of improved survival over outcomes reported in other studies evaluating surgery alone in this patient population was observed. The high pCR rates and durable responses observed may provide useful information for designing future clinical studies, including randomized trials investigating organ-preserving strategies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04006262.

makaleler.baslik: Comparison of External Oblique Intercostal Plane Block and Subcostal Transversus Abdominis Plane Block for Postoperative Analgesia After Open Radical Gastrectomy: A Single-Blind Randomized Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Açık Radikal Gastrektomi Sonrası EOIP ve scTAP Bloklarının Karşılaştırılması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 60 hastanın katıldığı tek merkezli randomize çalışmada, ilk 24 saatlik kümülatif morfin tüketimi EOIP grubunda 24,3±11,4 mg, scTAP grubunda ise 22,4±8,8 mg bulunmuş olup gruplar arasında istatistiksel olarak anlamlı fark saptanmamıştır (p=0,47). Postoperatif ağrı skorları, kurtarıcı analjezik ihtiyacı ve PONV oranları da benzerilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet: Background: Ultrasound-guided fascial plane blocks are increasingly incorporated into multimodal analgesia for upper abdominal surgery. Although both the external oblique intercostal plane (EOIP) block and the subcostal transversus abdominis plane (scTAP) block have been used for postoperative analgesia, evidence directly comparing their efficacy after open radical gastrectomy is lacking. We compared the postoperative analgesic efficacy of bilateral EOIP and bilateral scTAP blocks in patients undergoing open radical gastrectomy. Methods: In this prospective, single-center, randomized, patient-blinded trial, 60 adults undergoing elective open radical gastrectomy were randomly assigned to receive either a bilateral ultrasound-guided EOIP block or a bilateral scTAP block. The primary outcome was cumulative morphine consumption during the first 24 postoperative hours. Secondary outcomes included postoperative Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) scores, rescue analgesic requirements, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), and length of hospital stay. Results: Thirty patients were analyzed in each group. 24 h cumulative morphine consumption did not differ significantly between the EOIP and scTAP groups (24.3 ± 11.4 mg vs. 22.4 ± 8.8 mg, respectively; mean difference 1.9 mg, 95% confidence interval -3.10 to 6.97; p = 0.47). Morphine consumption at 2, 6, and 12 h also showed no statistically significant differences. Postoperative NRS scores showed no significant differences at any time point. Rescue analgesic requirements and the proportion of patients experiencing PONV episodes did not differ significantly between the groups. No complications were observed. Conclusions: Among patients undergoing open radical gastrectomy, no statistically significant differences were detected between bilateral EOIP and bilateral scTAP blocks in postoperative opioid consumption, pain scores, rescue analgesic requirements, or PONV. These findings do not establish equivalence or efficacy relative to standard care without a block and warrant confirmation in larger multicenter trials.

tez.baslik: Mide kanserli hastalarda neoadjuvan kemoterapinin postoperatif morbidite ve mortaliteye etkisi
tez.baslik_tr: Mide Kanserinde Neoadjuvan Kemoterapinin Postoperatif Etkisi
tez.kisa_ozet: 120 hastanın incelendiği retrospektif kohort çalışmasında, neoadjuvan kemoterapi alan grupta genel sağkalım anlamlı olarak daha uzun saptanmıştır (50,56 aya karşın 39,59 ay; p=0,022).
tez.ozet: Amaç: Bu çalışmada, mide kanseri nedeniyle opere edilen hastalarda neoadjuvan kemoterapi (NAKT) uygulamasının postoperatif morbidite ve mortalite üzerine etkisinin araştırılması amaçlanmıştır. Gereç ve Yöntem: Bu retrospektif kohort çalışmasına, Mersin Üniversitesi Genel Cerrahi Kliniği'nde mide kanseri tanısıyla opere edilen 120 hasta dahil edilmiştir. Hastalar preoperatif NAKT uygulanıp uygulanmamasına göre iki gruba ayrılarak karşılaştırılmıştır. Preoperatif dönemde yaş, cinsiyet, komorbidite (hipertansiyon, diyabet, kardiyak hastalık), vücut kitle indeksi, sigara-alkol kullanımı, ASA skoru, klinik TNM evresi, tümör lokalizasyonu, CRP, albumin, hematokrit, CEA ve CA19-9 değerleri ile görüntüleme bulguları (endoskopik ultrasonografi, PET-BT, tanısal laparoskopi) kayıt altına alınmıştır. Perioperatif parametreler olarak operasyon süresi, epidural analjezi uygulaması, perioperatif eritrosit süspansiyonu ihtiyacı, çoklu organ rezeksiyonu, gastrektomi tipi (subtotal/total) ve anastomoz şekli değerlendirilmiştir. Postoperatif dönemde komplikasyonlar Clavien-Dindo sınıflamasına göre ve yara yeri enfeksiyonu varlığı açısından incelenmiş; yoğun bakım yatış süreleri ve toplam hastane yatış süreleri kaydedilmiştir. Patolojik değerlendirmede çıkarılan ve metastatik lenf nodu sayısı, patolojik TNM evresi cerrahi sınır mesafeleri (proksimal ve distal), c-erbB-2 skoru, perinöral invazyon, lenfovasküler invazyon ve tümör tipi incelenmiştir. Ayrıca hastalara ait takip süresi, nüks, hastalıksız sağkalım ve genel sağkalım verileri analiz edilmiştir. İstatistiksel analizler R yazılımı kullanılarak gerçekleştirilmiştir. Sürekli değişkenler için Shapiro-Wilk testi, kategorik değişkenler için Mann-Whitney U testi uygulanmıştır. Kategorik değişkenlerin gruplar arasındaki dağılımı, beklenen hücre değerlerinin uygunluğuna göre ki-kare testi veya Fisher'in kesin testi ile değerlendirildi. Hastalıksız sağkalım ve genel sağkalım Kaplan-Meier yöntemi ile hesaplandı; gruplar arasındaki sağkalım farkı log-rank testi ile değerlendirildi. Hastalıksız sağkalım ve genel sağkalım üzerine etkili olabilecek bağımsız faktörlerin belirlenmesinde geriye doğru eleme yöntemi uygulanarak Çok Değişkenli Cox Regresyon Analizi ile değerlendirildi; sonuçlar hazard oranı (HR) ile %95 güven aralığı (GA) olarak sunuldu. İstatistiksel anlamlılık düzeyi p 0,05); NAKT alan grupta vücut kitle indeksi, albümin ve CEA düzeyleri anlamlı olarak daha yüksek, alkol vi kullanımı ise daha düşük bulunmuştur (p 0,05); lenfovasküler invazyon NAKT almayan grupta anlamlı olarak daha yüksek bulunmuştur (p=0,037).Genel sağkalım NAKT alan grupta anlamlı olarak daha uzun saptanmıştır (50,56 aya karşın 39,59 ay; p=0,022) hastalıksız sağkalım açısından ise gruplar arasında anlamlı fark bulunmamıştır (p=0,216). Çok değişkenli Cox regresyon analizinde toplam yatış süresi (HR=1,07; p<0,001) ve lenfovasküler invazyon (HR=2,62; p=0,006) genel sağkalım için bağımsız risk faktörleri olarak belirlenmiştir. Hastalıksız sağkalım için ileri patolojik evre (HR=13,98–27,11) bağımsız risk faktörü, iyi diferansiye histoloji (HR=0,28; p=0,034) ise koruyucu faktör olarak belirlenmiştir. Sonuç: Bu çalışma, lokal ileri mide adenokarsinomu nedeniyle ameliyat edilen hastalarda NAKT'nin postoperatif komplikasyonları olumsuz etkilemediğini ve hastanede yatış süresini olumlu yönde kısalttığını göstermiştir. NAKT'nin genel sağkalımı olumlu etkilediği görülmüş. Hastalıksız sağkalım ise NAKT'den etkilenmemiştir. Bulgularımız, NAKT'nin mide kanseri cerrahisinde güvenle uygulanabilecek bir tedavi yaklaşımı olduğunu desteklemektedir. Anahtar Kelimeler: Mide kanseri, neoadjuvan kemoterapi, gastrektomi, hastalıksız sağkalım, genel sağkalım, mortalite, morbidite

makaleler.baslik: Bariatric Surgery and Risk of Obesity-Related Cancer by Age and Sex.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Bariatrik Cerrahi ve Obezite İlişkili Kanser Riski
makaleler.kisa_ozet: NordOSCo verileriyle yapılan popülasyon tabanlı kohort çalışmasında, bariatrik cerrahi genel olarak obezite ilişkili kanser riskinde azalma ile ilişkilendirildi (aIRR 0,81; %95 CI 0,77-0,85). Karaciğer (aIRR 0,49) ve endometriyum (aIRR 0,51) kanserlerinde en güçlü ters ilişki görülürken, pankreas kanseri riski arttı.
makaleler.ozet:
IMPORTANCE: Obesity is associated with elevated risks for multiple cancers. How bariatric surgery influences these risks across age and sex is insufficiently understood.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between bariatric surgery and obesity-related cancer (breast, endometrial, ovarian, esophageal adenocarcinoma, liver, pancreatic, colon, rectal, kidney, and multiple myeloma) and whether this association varies by age and sex.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This population-based cohort study within the Nordic Obesity Surgery Cohort (NordOSCo) included individuals aged 18 to 59 years with an obesity record in Denmark, Finland, or Sweden from 1992 to 2023. Prospectively collected data on exposure, outcomes, and confounders were obtained from well-maintained national registries. Follow-up continued until cancer diagnosis, death, emigration, or December 31, 2023. These data were analyzed from December 2025 to April 2026.
EXPOSURE: Bariatric surgery vs no surgery among individuals with obesity.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was incidence of obesity-related cancers. Risks were compared using crude and multivariable-adjusted incidence rate ratios (aIRR) with 95% CIs derived from Poisson regression adjusted for age, sex, calendar year, country, and obesity- and lifestyle-related comorbidities. Effect modification by age group (18-39 vs 40-59 years) and sex (female vs male) was evaluated using interaction terms.
RESULTS: Among 784 105 individuals with obesity (569 266 women [73%] and 214 839 men [27%]), 99 614 underwent bariatric surgery. Surgery was associated with a lower risk of obesity-related cancer overall (aIRR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.77-0.85). The magnitude of risk reduction did not differ by age group (individuals aged 18 to 39 years: aIRR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.72-0.88 and individuals aged 40 to 59 years: aIRR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.78-0.86) (P for interaction = .88). Associations for non-sex-specific cancers were similar in men and women (P for interaction = .50). For individual cancers, the strongest inverse associations were observed for liver cancer (aIRR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.34-0.70), endometrial cancer (aIRR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.45-0.59), and ovarian cancer (aIRR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.60-0.87). In contrast, pancreatic cancer risk was increased after surgery, particularly among younger adults (aIRR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.44-3.39; P = .01).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, bariatric surgery was associated with a lower long-term risk of obesity-related cancers, with similar associations across age groups and sexes. These findings suggest that the long-term oncologic benefits of bariatric surgery apply broadly across age groups and sexes, supporting equitable access to bariatric surgery for patients with obesity.

makaleler.baslik: Artificial intelligence in metabolic and bariatric surgery: current applications and future direction from the ASMBS Emerging Technology and Procedures Committee.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Metabolik ve Bariatrik Cerrahide Yapay Zeka Uygulamaları
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Derleme çalışmasında, bariatrik cerrahinin preoperatif, intraoperatif, postoperatif ve idari alanlarında yapay zekanın mevcut kanıtları ve önerileri sentezlendi. Çoğu kanıt retrospektif ve tek merkezli olup, klinik rol, validasyon ve veri güvenliği gibi zorluklar vurgulandı.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated across the perioperative continuum of metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS), yet adoption is outpacing specialty-specific guidance on safe, effective, and equitable implementation.
OBJECTIVES: To synthesize current evidence on AI applications in MBS, identify key implementation challenges, and provide recommendations for responsible clinical adoption.
SETTING: American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery (ASMBS) Emerging Technology and Procedures (ET&P) Committee.
METHODS: Surgeon-led narrative review of published literature on AI in MBS and relevant adjacent surgical and chronic disease fields, organized by preoperative, intraoperative, postoperative, and administrative domains, with recommendations developed by committee consensus.
RESULTS: Preoperatively, machine learning models outperform conventional risk indices for predicting complications and readmission and can forecast long-term weight trajectories. Intraoperatively, computer vision systems recognize procedural steps in sleeve gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with accuracy comparable to expert annotators, and AI-enabled video and virtual reality platforms support objective skills assessment. Postoperatively, wearable-based remote monitoring and predictive models may identify early deterioration, weight regain, and comorbidity recurrence. Administratively, ambient AI scribes, prior authorization automation, and operating room scheduling may reduce clerical burden. Most evidence remains retrospective and single-center. Key challenges include large language model hallucination, automation bias and deskilling, algorithmic bias, and data privacy. Eight operational recommendations address clinical role, MBS-specific validation, equity auditing, documentation, governance, technical safety, workflow integration, and learning health systems.
CONCLUSIONS: AI can enhance the safety, efficiency, and scalability of MBS when clinician-led, rigorously validated, equitable, and transparent. Prospective, multicenter evaluation is needed before broad adoption.
