makaleler.baslik: Endoscopic closure technique performance for iatrogenic perforation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: İatrojenik Perforasyonda Endoskopik Kapatma Tekniklerinin Performansı
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 795 perforasyonun değerlendirildiği meta-analizde pooled teknik başarı %91,5 ve klinik başarı %86,3 olarak bulundu. TTSCs, OTSCs ve OTSS arasında başarı oranları açısından anlamlı fark saptanmadı (p=0,24).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Perforation is the most feared endoscopy-related adverse event. Various closure techniques are available, including through-the-scope clips (TTSCs), over-the-scope clips (OTSCs), and over-the-scope suturing (OTSS). Given the lack of comparative performance estimates, we sought to systematically appraise TTSC, OTSC, and OTSS performance for iatrogenic perforation.
METHODS: MEDLINE and Embase were independently searched between June 1947 and January 2024 for citations evaluating TTSC, OTSC, or OTSS performance. Technical success was defined as complete apposition of the borders of the defect with visual confirmation. Clinical success was defined as technical success without further intervention. Pooled estimates using random-effects modeling were generated and stratified by closure modality, location, perforation etiology, and time.
RESULTS: Thirty-seven citations assessing 795 perforations were included. Pooled technical and clinical success were 91.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 87.9-94.1; I 2 = 26%) and 86.3% (95% CI, 81.9-89.8; I 2 = 39%). Technical success of TTSCs, OTSCs, and OTSS was 89.3% (95% CI, 82.6-93.6), 90.7% (95% CI, 86.0-93.9), and 94.9% (95% CI, 83.8-98.5; P = .53), respectively. Clinical success of TTSCs, OTSCs, and OTSS was 85.3% (95% CI, 77.9-90.6), 86.2% (95% CI, 80.4-90.5) and 94.9% (95% CI, 83.8-98.5) (P = .24). Clinical success was significantly higher for tissue resection-related perforations (P = .02) and perforations in the stomach (P < .04); no difference in clinical success was identified when stratifying by closure modality and time (all P > .05).
CONCLUSIONS: TTSCs, OTSCs, and OTSS are effective for iatrogenic perforation management, especially in tissue resection-related perforations and perforations in the stomach. No difference in performance was identified on the basis of closure modality or time.

makaleler.baslik: In older adults, "mild" by GCS does not mean low risk: Multicenter study of 1,157 patients with mild TBI and acute subdural hematoma.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Hafif TBI ve Akut Subdural Hematomlu Yaşlı Hastalarda Çok Merkezli Sonuçlar
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 1.157 hastanın incelendiği retrospektif çalışmada, yaşlı hastalarda toplam mortalite %10 olarak bulundu. Yaşlılarda sağkalımı etkileyen bağımsız faktörler arasında önceden belirlenmiş talimatlar ve orta hat kayması yer aldı.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Acute traumatic subdural hematoma (SDH) is the most common intracranial injury in mild TBI (mTBI), particularly in older adults. However, the relationship of patient and brain computed tomography (CT) characteristics with outcomes remains poorly described in a contemporary cohort. This study aims to characterize outcomes in younger and older adults with mTBI and isolated acute SDH.
METHODS: This was a 10-center, retrospective cohort study of adult traumas with emergency department Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 13 to 15 and acute traumatic SDH on initial brain CT ('22-'23). Trauma registry, EHR, and Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) data were collected through automated and manual methods. The primary outcome was total mortality (TM=death+hospice discharge); the sample was stratified by 18 to 64 versus older than or equal to 65 years. Multivariable backward selection logistic regression examined 21 demographic, injury, and brain CT covariates.
RESULTS: In total, 1,157 patients were included (18-64 y: 28%; ≥65 y: 72%; 58% transferred in). Median [IQR] non-head ISS was 1 [1-5] in 18 to 64 years, and 1 [1-2] in older than or equal to 65 years. Ten percent had neurosurgical intervention (18-64 y: 8%; ≥65 y: 11%). TM was higher in older than or equal to 65 years than 18 to 64 years (10% vs. 3%). Compared with older than or equal to 65 years, 18 to 64 years were discharged home more frequently (78% vs. 51%) and to hospice less frequently (2% vs. 7%). In 18 to 64 years, factors associated with TM were race, advance directive, functional dependence, ISS, more midline shift, and thicker SDH (too few TMs for adjusted models). In older than or equal to 65 years, factors independently associated with TM were advance directive (aOR [95% CI]: 11.8 [2.9-49.0]), male sex (3.0 [1.3-7.0]), midline shift (1.8 [1.3-2.6]), shock index (1.5 [1.1-2.1]), and worsening SDH on follow-up CT (2.9 [1.3-6.6]).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite presenting as "mild", these data highlight that older adults with SDH have high TM and should continue to receive the highest-level care with timely goals-of-care discussions. The association between advance directives and TM should be interpreted within the context of baseline vulnerability and preinjury treatment preferences, not as a biological mortality predictor.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, prognostic/epidemiological.

turk.baslik: Predictors of surgical intervention and timing of ileus presentation in patients with adhesive small bowel obstruction.
turk.baslik_tr: Adheziv İleusta Cerrahi Girişim ve Sunum Zamanı Prediktörleri
turk.kisa_ozet: 450 hastanın incelendiği çalışmada, 302 hasta cerrahi müdahale gerektirdi. Cerrahi grupta operasyon süresi uzun (4,3 saate karşı 3,1 saat, p=0,003) ve ileus başvuru süresi daha kısa (5,5 aya karşı 6,8 ay, p=0,002) bulundu.
turk.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Adhesive small bowel obstruction remains a common long-term complication following abdominal surgery and continues to represent a significant cause of morbidity and healthcare utilization. While several factors contributing to adhesion formation have been described, determinants influencing both the need for surgical intervention and the timing of clinical presentation are not yet fully understood. This study aimed to identify factors associated with surgical management in patients presenting with adhesive ileus after a single prior abdominal operation and to evaluate the relationship between operative duration and the timing of ileus onset.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 450 patients (n=450) diagnosed with adhesive ileus at a tertiary care center between January 1, 2021 and January 1, 2026. Patients with mechanical obstruction or multiple prior abdominal surgeries were excluded. Patients were categorized into operative (n=302) and conservative (n=148) management groups. Baseline characteristics, including age, sex, and American Society of Anesthesiologists scores, were comparable between groups (p>0.05). Clinical variables such as type of prior surgery, operative duration, surgical approach, contamination status, and time to ileus presentation were analyzed. Statistical analyses included an independent samples t-test, Chi-square test, Pearson correlation analysis, and multivariate logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of the 450 patients, 302 (67.1%) required surgical intervention. Operative duration was significantly longer in the operative group compared to the conservative group (4.3±1.8 vs. 3.1±1.6 h, p=0.003). Open surgery (75% vs. 52%, p=0.037) and contaminated surgical fields (78% vs. 60%, p=0.030) were more frequent in the operative group. The time to ileus presentation was significantly shorter in patients requiring surgery (5.5±1.9 vs. 6.8±2.1 months, p=0.002). A significant inverse relationship was observed between operative duration and time to ileus presentation (r=-0.32, p<0.05).
CONCLUSION: Operative duration, surgical approach, and intraoperative contamination are important determinants of surgical management in adhesive ileus. The inverse relationship between operative duration and time to presentation suggests that increased surgical burden may contribute to an earlier onset of clinically significant obstruction. These findings highlight the potential value of surgical factors in risk stratification and post-operative surveillance.

tez.baslik: Komplike ve komplike olmayan akut apandisit durumlarının ayırt edilmesinde yapay sinir ağı modellerinin uygulanabilirliği
tez.baslik_tr: Akut Apandisitte Komplike Durumların Yapay Sinir Ağları ile Ayrımı
tez.kisa_ozet: 259 hastanın dâhil edildiği çalışmada, multimodal yapay sinir ağı modeli komplike apandisiti öngörmede Model A için AUC 0,937 ve Model B için AUC 0,958 performans gösterdi. Semptom süresi en baskın prediktör olarak saptandı.
tez.ozet: ÖZET KOMPLİKE VE KOMPLİKE OLMAYAN AKUT APANDİSİT DURUMLARININ AYIRT EDİLMESİNDE YAPAY SİNİR AĞI MODELLERİNİN UYGULANABİLİRLİĞİ Amaç. Akut apandisit (AA), dünya genelinde en sık karşılaşılan cerrahi acillerden biridir. Komplike (gangrenöz, perfore, periapendiküler apse veya plastronlu) ve komplike olmayan (kataral, flegmonöz/süpüratif) formların preoperatif ayrımı; tedavi stratejisinin belirlenmesi, cerrahi zamanlamanın yapılması ve postoperatif yönetim açısından kritiktir. Mevcut klinik, laboratuvar ve görüntüleme yöntemlerinin tek başına tanısal performansı bu ayrımda sınırlı kalmaktadır. Çalışmanın birincil amacı; klinik–laboratuvar değişkenleri, bilgisayarlı tomografi (BT) görüntülerinden çıkarılan radyomik öznitelikleri ve BT raporlarından doğal dil işleme (NLP) ile çıkarılan yapılandırılmış değişkenleri birleştiren üç dallı bir multimodal yapay sinir ağı modelinin (MultiModalNet), intraoperatif komplike–komplike olmayan ayrımını preoperatif olarak öngörmedeki uygulanabilirliğini değerlendirmektir. İkincil amaç olarak aynı modelleme yaklaşımı histopatolojik sınıflama referansına göre de değerlendirilerek iki referans standardı karşılaştırılmıştır. Gereç ve Yöntem. T.C. Sağlık Bilimleri Üniversitesi İstanbul Başakşehir Çam ve Sakura Şehir Hastanesi Genel Cerrahi Kliniği'nde 20.03.2025–20.03.2026 tarihleri arasında akut apandisit ön tanısıyla apendektomi uygulanmış erişkin (≥18 yaş) hastalar üzerinde yürütülen tek merkezli, prospektif bir çalışmadır. Prospektif olarak değerlendirilen 407 hastanın 97'sinde BT'nin dış merkezde çekilmiş olması, 31 hastaya kontrastsız BT çekilmiş olması, 15 hastanın görüntü kalitesinin segmentasyona uygun olmaması (8 hasta komplike apandisit nitelikli olup BT'de apendiks duvar bütünlüğü bozulmuş ve çevresi tamamen apse ile kaplanmış olduğundan güvenilir bir ROI sınırı belirlenememiş; 3 hastada BT kesitlerinin bazıları HBYS'ye eksik aktarılmış; 2 hastada solunum ve hareket artefaktı segmentasyonu olanaksız kılmış; 1 hastada eş zamanlı over kist rüptürü ve 1 hastada eş zamanlı over torsiyonu klinik tabloyu apandisitten farklılaştırmış) ve 5 hastada gebelik nedeniyle BT çekilmemiş olması gerekçeleriyle bu hastalar çalışmadan çıkarılmış; sonuçta 259 hasta analize dâhil edilmiştir (249'una laparoskopik, 10'una açık apendektomi uygulandı). Birincil sonuç değişkeni, ameliyat sırasında cerrahi ekip tarafından doğrudan gözlenen makroskopik tablodur: 101 olgu (%39,0) komplike, 158 olgu (%61,0) komplike olmayan olarak sınıflanmıştır. Histopatolojik sınıflama (gangrenöz/perfore: 37/259; %14,3) ikincil referans olarak korunmuştur. Yirmi sekiz klinik/laboratuvar değişkeni, 3D Slicer ile manuel apendiks segmentasyonu üzerinden PyRadiomics ile çıkarılan 107 radyomik öznitelik ve Türkçe BT raporlarından kural tabanlı NLP ile çıkarılan dokuz öznitelik toplanmıştır. İntraoperatif hedef için iki konfigürasyon tanımlanmıştır: Model A (BT raporu yok) yalnızca klinik ve radyomik öznitelikleri; Model B (BT raporu var) klinik, radyomik ve NLP modalitelerinin tamamını bütünleştirir. Üç aşamalı öznitelik seçim hattı (Pearson |ρ| ≥ 0,05 → VIF ≤ 10 → LassoCV) uygulanmış; veri seti stratifiye olarak %70 eğitim, %20 doğrulama, %10 bağımsız test (n ≈ 26) setine bölünmüş; SMOTE yalnızca eğitim alt-kümesinde uygulanmıştır. Önerilen MultiModalNet, altı klasik makine öğrenmesi algoritmasıyla (lojistik regresyon, rastgele orman, XGBoost, destek vektör makinesi, karar ağacı, Gaussian naive Bayes) karşılaştırılmış; tüm hat beş bağımsız rastgele tohum [42, 123, 456, 789, 2024] üzerinde tekrar çalıştırılmıştır. Bulgular. Popülasyonun %62,9'u (n = 163) erkek, %37,1'i (n = 96) kadın; medyan yaş 33 (Q1–Q3: 26–46) yıldı. Komplike grupta semptom süresi (medyan 72 vs 24 saat), CRP (159,9 vs 13,7 mg/L), nötrofil/lenfosit oranı (NLO; 7,3 vs 4,7), total bilirubin (0,9 vs 0,6 mg/dL), defans (%22,8 vs %6,3) ve rebound (%48,5 vs %25,3) anlamlı yüksek; albümin (43 vs 47 g/L) belirgin biçimde düşüktü (tümü için p < 0,001). Bağımsız test setinde MultiModalNet performansı beş tohum ortalaması olarak Model A için AUC-ROC = 0,937 ± 0,046 (duyarlılık 0,880; özgüllük 0,975; F1 0,914), Model B için AUC-ROC = 0,958 ± 0,026 (duyarlılık 0,900; özgüllük 0,963; F1 0,919) olarak ölçülmüştür. Lojistik regresyon vekil tahminci ile 5-katlı çapraz doğrulamada Model A için CV AUC = 0,950 ± 0,006; Model B için CV AUC = 0,968 ± 0,003 değerlerine ulaşılmıştır. Alvarado skorunun tek başına intraoperatif komplike apandisit öngörüsündeki performansı AUC = 0,591 (%95 GA: 0,523 0,659); klasik eşik olan ≥7 değerinde duyarlılık yalnızca 0,307 idi. SHAP analizinde semptom süresi (ortalama |SHAP| = 0,189) baskın prediktör; modalite düzeyinde klinik %62, NLP %26, radyomik %12 katkı oranıyla öne çıkmıştır. İkincil histopatolojik konfigürasyonda model AUC = 0,856 ± 0,007 ile belirgin biçimde daha düşük performans sergilemiştir. Sonuç. Klinik, radyomik ve NLP özniteliklerini birleştiren multimodal yapay sinir ağı, preoperatif dönemde intraoperatif komplike akut apandisit ayrımını yüksek tanısal doğruluk, duyarlılık, özgüllük ve negatif prediktif değer ile öngörebilmektedir. Modelin pratik açıdan kritik bir avantajı, BT raporunun erişilebilir olmadığı koşullarda dahi yüksek performans göstermesidir. Tek merkezli tasarım, sınırlı pozitif olgu sayısı ve harici doğrulama eksikliği gibi kısıtlılıklar nedeniyle modelin klinik uygulamaya alınabilmesi için çok merkezli prospektif harici doğrulama çalışmalarına ihtiyaç vardır. Anahtar Kelimeler: Akut apandisit; komplike apandisit; intraoperatif sınıflama; yapay sinir ağı; multimodal öğrenme; radyomik; 3D Slicer; makine öğrenmesi; bilgisayarlı tomografi; doğal dil işleme.

makaleler.baslik: Rapid versus slow puncture in endoscopic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy: a multicenter randomized crossover trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: EUS Eşliğinde Karaciğer Biyopsisinde Hızlı ve Yavaş İğne Teknikleri
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 62 örneğin analiz edildiği çok merkezli randomize çapraz çalışmada, hızlı delme tekniği geleneksel yavaş delme tekniğine kıyasla portal trakt sayısını (ortalama fark 2,39; %95 CI 1,50-3,27) ve toplam örnek uzunluğunu (ortalama fark 15,19 mm; %95 CI 9,65-20,74) anlamlı derecede artırmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy (EUS-LB) is increasingly used for hepatic histologic assessment; however, optimal technical approaches remain undefined. This prospective, multicenter clinical study aimed to compare tissue acquisition and safety between the rapid and slow puncture techniques for EUS-LB.
METHODS: This was a multicenter randomized crossover study. Patients undergoing EUS-LB were randomized to receive both rapid puncture and slow puncture techniques in alternating sequence during the same session. The primary outcomes were the number of complete portal tracts (CPTs) and total specimen length (TSL). The secondary outcomes were diagnostic adequacy and adverse events. Linear mixed models and generalized linear mixed models were used to evaluate the technical performance.
RESULTS: A total of 62 specimens were analyzed. Compared with the conventional slow puncture technique, rapid puncture significantly increased CPTs (mean difference 2.39; 95%CI 1.50-3.27), as well as TSL (mean difference 15.19 mm; 95%CI 9.65-20.74), with corresponding improvements in diagnostic adequacy (odds ratio 16.27, 95%CI 2.41-109.97). Time period and center were not statistically significantly associated with the outcomes. No severe adverse events were reported.
CONCLUSION: The modified rapid puncture technique was associated with improved specimen quality in EUS-LB. These findings support its potential utility in clinical practice; however, further validation in larger and more diverse populations is warranted.

makaleler.baslik: Incidence of parastomal hernia after open versus minimally invasive surgery: a comparative systematic review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Açık ve Minimal İnvaziv Cerrahi Sonrası Parastomal Herni İnsidansı
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Toplam 1480 hastanın dahil edildiği 6 çalışmanın meta-analizinde, laparoskopik reeksiyonlar sonrasında açık cerrahiye kıyasla klinik olarak saptanan parastomal herni oranlarının daha yüksek olma eğiliminde olduğu görülmüştür (RR 1,89; %95 CI 1,39-2,58).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Peristomal bulging and external stoma prolapse are the most common long-term complications following stoma formation. This systematic review aims to describe available evidence on the incidence of parastomal hernia, subcutaneous prolapse and external stomal prolapse following open versus minimally invasive intestinal resections with definitive stoma formation.
METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, a literature search was performed to include studies published in the last 15 years on intestinal resections with a definitive ileostomy or colostomy formation and a follow-up of more than 12 months, reporting on PSH and/or subcutaneous prolapse and/or external stoma prolapse after laparoscopic or robotic, and open surgery. The incidence of PSH after open versus minimally invasive surgery was the primary outcome, and secondary outcomes included other stoma-related complications such as subcutaneous stoma prolapse and external stoma prolapse, and outcomes.
RESULTS: In total six studies (one randomised controlled trial and five observational studies) on 1480 patients with a definitive stoma were included (731 open, 749 laparoscopic). All studies reported PSH as an outcome, no study reported the incidence of subcutaneous prolapse and one study reported on external stoma prolapse. There was consistent trend toward higher PSH rates following laparoscopic resections, both in clinically (RR 1.89 (95% CI 1.39-2.58)) and radiologically (RR 1.70 (95% CI 0.89-3.28)) assessed hernias.
CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive intestinal resection may be associated with a higher incidence of PSH than open surgery, but the certainty of the evidence is very low. Subcutaneous prolapse is seldom recognised as a distinct form of stoma herniation. Clear differentiation is essential, as these conditions differ in their underlying mechanisms and management.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251026395.

makaleler.baslik: Bayesian network meta-analysis comparing efficacy of surgical gastrojejunostomy, endoscopic stenting, and EUS-guided gastroenterostomy for malignant gastric outlet obstruction.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Malign Gastrik Çıkış Obstrüksiyonunda Tedavi Yöntemlerinin Meta-Analizi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 15 çalışmayı içeren Bayesian network meta-analizinde, malign gastric outlet obstruction hastalarında EUS-guided gastroenterostomy S-GJ'ye göre daha yüksek klinik başarı sağladı (RR 1,38; %95 CrI 1,15-1,88). Endoskopik yaklaşımlar oral alım ve hastane kalış süresini kısalttı, ancak ES grubunda reintervention daha sık görüldü.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Malignant gastric outlet obstruction (GOO) substantially impairs quality of life in patients with advanced malignancies. Surgical gastrojejunostomy (S-GJ), endoscopic stenting (ES), and EUS-guided gastroenterostomy (EUS-GE) are the principal palliative options. We performed a Bayesian network meta-analysis to compare their efficacy and safety.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through April 13, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and eligible comparative cohort studies comparing at least two interventions in adults with malignant GOO were included. Bayesian network meta-analysis was performed, and treatments were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA).
RESULTS: Fifteen studies (7 RCTs and 8 cohort studies; 827 patients) were included. EUS-GE achieved higher clinical success than S-GJ (risk ratio [RR] 1.38, 95% credible interval [CrI] 1.15-1.88; SUCRA 0.98), and ES was also superior to S-GJ (RR 1.18, 95% CrI 1.01-1.49). Reintervention was more frequent with ES than with S-GJ (RR 3.61, 95% CrI 1.43-14.51) or EUS-GE (RR 7.56, 95% CrI 2.02-38.14), whereas EUS-GE ranked highest for durability (SUCRA 0.93). Both endoscopic approaches shortened time to oral intake and hospital stay compared with S-GJ. No statistically significant between-treatment differences were identified for adverse events, 30-day mortality, or overall survival.
CONCLUSIONS: EUS-GE was associated with a favorable balance of efficacy, durability, and recovery and may represent a promising minimally invasive alternative in centers with appropriate expertise. ES provides rapid recovery but is associated with more frequent reintervention, whereas S-GJ remains an established option. Additional direct randomized comparisons are needed to define the optimal palliative strategy.

makaleler.baslik: Efficacy, safety, and cost of immediate versus on-demand endoscopic necrosectomy in infected necrotizing pancreatitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Nekrotizan Pankreatitte Erken ve On-Demand Endoskopik Nekrozektomi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 215 hastayı içeren 4 RCT'nin meta-analizinde, EUS kılavuzluğunda drenaj sonrası erken ve on-demand nekrozektomi teknik başarı ve klinik başarı açısından benzer bulundu (RR 1,17; %95 CI 0,98-1,40). Erken nekrozektomi, nekrozektomi uygulanan hasta oranını artırdı (RR 1,65; %95 CI 1,13-2,41).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided drainage is the standard of care for walled-off necrosis (WON); however, the optimal timing of subsequent endoscopic necrosectomy remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing immediate versus on-demand necrosectomy following EUS-guided drainage.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through March 2026 for RCTs comparing immediate (≤ 72 h) versus on-demand necrosectomy in adults with necrotizing pancreatitis. Primary outcomes were technical success, clinical success, and the proportion of patients undergoing necrosectomy. Secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, costs, need for percutaneous or multigate drainage, and adverse events. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Four RCTs comprising 215 patients, of whom 192 (89.3%) had WON, were included. Immediate and on-demand approaches demonstrated similar technical success (RR 1.01, 95%CI 0.98-1.05) and clinical success (RR 1.17, 95%CI 0.98-1.40). Immediate necrosectomy was associated with a higher proportion of patients undergoing necrosectomy (RR 1.65, 95%CI 1.13-2.41). No significant differences were observed in length of hospital stay, costs, need for additional drainage, procedure- or disease-related adverse events, mortality, bleeding, stent migration, or pneumoperitoneum.
CONCLUSIONS: Immediate endoscopic necrosectomy did not demonstrate a consistent clinical advantage over an on-demand approach. Low- to very-low-certainty evidence suggests little or no difference in clinical efficacy or safety outcomes, while very-low-certainty evidence suggests that immediate necrosectomy may increase the proportion of patients undergoing necrosectomy. However, the magnitude and clinical significance of this effect remain uncertain. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of randomized trials, modest sample sizes, and low or very low certainty of evidence for several outcomes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261366884).

makaleler.baslik: Predictors of clinical success in endoscopic ultrasound-guided drainage of postoperative pancreatic fluid collections.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Postoperatif Pankreas Koleksiyonlarında EUS Drenajı
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Pankreas cerrahisi sonrası gelişen koleksiyonlar nedeniyle EUS eşliğinde drenaj yapılan 265 hastanın retrospektif çalışmasında, klinik başarı %73 olarak bildirilmiştir. Distal pankerektomi, pankreatikoduodenektomiye kıyasla daha düşük klinik başarı şansı ile ilişkilidir (OR 0,53; p=0,04).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided drainage is increasingly used for the management of postoperative pancreatic fluid collections (POPFC). We aimed to identify factors associated with clinical success, and to perform exploratory analyses of outcomes stratified by surgery type and stent type.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study including patients who underwent EUS-guided drainage of POPFC following pancreatic surgery between 2014 and August 2024 at three academic centers. The primary outcome was clinical success, defined as combined radiological and clinical resolution without the need for percutaneous or surgical step-up intervention.
RESULTS: A total of 265 patients were included (mean age 64±14 years; 57% male; 52% underwent drainage ≤14 days after surgery, necrotic component in 51%). Clinical success was achieved in 194 patients (73%; 95% CI 67.5-78.1%), including 160 (60%; 95% CI 54.5-66.3%) after a single procedure and 34 after additional endoscopic reinterventions, while 20 patients (7.6%; 95% CI 4.4-10.7%) required percutaneous or surgical step-up. Distal pancreatectomy, compared with pancreaticoduodenectomy, was associated with a higher rate of reintervention (32% vs. 20%, p=0.02) and independently associated with lower odds of clinical success (odds ratio 0.53, 95% confidence interval 0.29-0.98; p=0.04).
CONCLUSIONS: EUS-guided drainage for POPFC appears effective, with an acceptable safety profile in expert centers, achieving clinical resolution in the majority of patients. Distal pancreatectomy was associated with a more complex treatment course. These findings support the use of EUS-guided drainage as a central component in the management of POPFC.

turk.baslik: Lemmel syndrome: A single-center cohort and diagnostic considerations.
turk.baslik_tr: Lemmel Sendromu: Tek Merkezli Kohort ve Tanısal Yaklaşım
turk.kisa_ozet: 12 hastanın incelendiği retrospektif çalışmada, Lemmel sendromunun obstrüktif sarılığa neden olabileceği gösterildi. USG tanıda yetersiz kalırken, BT ve MRCP tanıda kilit rol oynadı ve hastaların çoğu endoskopik olarak yönetildi.
turk.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: Lemmel syndrome is an uncommon cause of obstructive jaundice resulting from extrinsic compression of the common bile duct by a periampullary duodenal diverticulum (PAD) in the absence of choledocholithiasis. Due to its non-specific clinical presentation, diagnosis may be delayed or misinterpreted.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted on 12 patients diagnosed with Lemmel syndrome at a single tertiary center between 2022 and 2024. Demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, laboratory findings, imaging modalities [ultrasonography (USG), computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP)], endoscopic interventions, and outcomes were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: The cohort included 12 patients with a mean age of 70±9 years. All patients presented with clinical or biochemical evidence of obstructive jaundice. USG frequently failed to establish the diagnosis, whereas CT and particularly MRCP demonstrated the anatomical relationship between the PAD and the biliary tree. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography served both diagnostic and therapeutic purposes, with biliary stenting performed when indicated. Most patients improved with conservative and/or endoscopic management.
CONCLUSION: Lemmel syndrome should be considered in elderly patients with unexplained obstructive jaundice. Cross-sectional imaging, particularly MRCP, plays a key role in diagnosis, while endoscopic intervention remains central to management.

tez.baslik: Laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahide dren şart mı? Prospektif randomize klinik çalışma
tez.baslik_tr: Laparoskopik Kolorektal Cerrahide Rutin Dren Kullanımı
tez.kisa_ozet: Laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahi geçiren 59 hastanın randomize edildiği çalışmada, rutin dren kullanımı ile drensiz yaklaşım arasında komplikasyonlar, reoperasyon oranları ve hastanede kalış süresi açısından anlamlı fark saptanmadı (p>0,05).
tez.ozet: Amaç: Laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahi sonrası rutin intraabdominal dren kullanımının yararı tartışma konusudur. Bu çalışma laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahisinde dren kullanımının postoperatif erken dönem klinik sonuçlar, komplikasyon oranları, hastanede kalış süresini prospektif randomize çalışmayla değerlendirmeyi amaçladık. Gereç ve Yöntem: Çalışmamız 01/12/2024 – 01/12/2025 tarihleri arasında S.B.Ü Gazi Yaşargil Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi Genel Cerrahi kliniğinde yürütülmüştür. Laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahi uygulanan toplam 59 hasta randomizasyon yöntemiyle iki gruba ayrılmıştır: Grup 1 (drensiz, n=27) ve Grup 2 (drenli, n=32). Drensiz grupta postoperatif 1. gün, 3. gün ve 5. günlerde, Girişimsel Radyoloji Kliniği tarafından tüm hastalar intraabdominal koleksiyon veya apse açısından batın ultrasonografisi ile değerlendirildi; apse veya koleksiyon saptanan hastalara perkütan dren yerleştirildi. Demografik veriler, komorbidite durumu, operasyon detayları, laboratuvar parametreleri, patolojik sonuçlar, T (tümör) ve N (lenf nodu) evrelemesi, ASA skorları, reoperasyon oranları, postoperatif komplikasyonlar, hastanede kalış süresi ile gaz ve gaita çıkış süreleri kaydedildi. İstatistiksel analizler SPSS 24.0 programı kullanılarak gerçekleştirildi. P değeri 0,05). Preoperatif labaratuvar değerleri (hemoglobin, CEA, CA19-9 vb.) iki grup arasında benzerdi (p>0,05). Postoperatif 1. Günde, dren yerleştirilen hastaların 24'ünde drenden ortalama 100 cc sero-hemorajik mayi drenajı olduğu saptandı. Perkütan dren ihtiyacı, drensiz grupta 2 hastada izlenmesine rağmen gruplar arasında istatistiksel olarak anlamlı fark saptanmadı (p=0,205). Reoperasyon oranı, postoperatif ileus, servis ve yoğun bakım yatış süreleri ile gaz ve gaita çıkış süreleri açısından gruplar arasında istatistiksel olarak anlamlı fark gözlenmedi (p>0,05). Majör komplikasyon oranları gruplar arasında benzer bulundu (p=0,273). Patolojik tanı dağılımı ile T ve N evreleri bakımından anlamlı farklılık izlenmedi (p>0,05). Sonuç: Çalışmamız, laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahi uygulanan hastalarda rutin dren kullanımının postoperatif klinik, radyolojik ve patolojik sonuçlar açısından anlamlı bir üstünlük sağlamadığını ortaya koymuştur. Elde edilen bulgular, dren kullanımının rutin bir uygulama olmaktan ziyade, intraoperatif bulgular, anastomoz güvenliği, kontaminasyon riski ve hasta özellikleri gibi bireysel faktörler göz önünde bulundurularak seçilmiş olgularda sınırlandırılmasının uygun olabileceğini göstermektedir. Anahtar Kelimeler: İntraabdominal dren, İntraabdominal koleksiyon, Laparaskopik kolorektal cerrahi.

makaleler.baslik: Robotic Simulation Training in Reducing the Learning Gap Between Expert Surgeons and Novice Trainees: A Prospective Single-Blinded Study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Robotik Simülasyon Eğitimi Uzmanlar ve Acemiler Arasındaki Beceriyi Kapatıyor
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 20 katılımcı ile yapılan prospektif çalışmada, standardize robotik simülasyon eğitimi sonrasında cerrahi asistanlar ile uzman cerrahların GEARS skorları arasında anlamlı fark bulunmadı (p=0,489). Bu bulgu, erken dönem robotik eğitimin müfredata entegrasyonunu desteklemektedir.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: Robotic-assisted surgery is increasingly adopted across surgical disciplines, yet structured training paradigms for novice trainees remain limited. Whether simulation-based robotic training can narrow the technical skill gap between experienced surgeons and trainees with varying levels of surgical experience is not well established. We aim to evaluate whether novice trainees can achieve comparable robotic suturing proficiency to expert surgeons following a standardised robotic simulation training programme, and to characterise the perceived learning curves across cohorts of varying surgical experience.
DESIGN: A prospective, single-blinded study was conducted at Woodlands Hospital, Singapore, using the Cornerstone Robotics Sentire Surgical System.
SETTING: Following simulation training modules, participants performed a standardised robotic suturing task. Two blinded assessors independently scored performance using the validated Global Evaluative Assessment of Robotic Skills (GEARS) instrument. Task completion time and participant self-assessment questionnaire scores were collected as secondary outcomes.
PARTICIPANTS: Four different cohorts with 5 participants each were recruited: Consultant surgeons (CS), Surgical Residents (SR), Non-surgical trainees (NST) and Year-5 Medical Students (M5). All participants were naïve to robotic surgery.
RESULTS: Mean total GEARS scores 26.4, 23.5, 19.2 and 13.7 (out of 30) in the CS, SR, NST and M5 groups respectively. There was no significant difference in scores between CS and SR group (p=0.489) but scores were significantly lower for NST and M5 when compared to the CS (p=0.013 and p<0.001). Median task completion times were: 5.92, 5.87, 9.75 and 14.0 minutes in the CS, SR, NST and M5 group respectively. Only the M5 timings were significantly longer compared to CS (p=0.08). Self-reported questionnaire scores showed a similar hierarchical pattern.
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic simulation training can potentially narrow the technical skills gap between expert surgeons and trainees, particularly for surgical residents. These findings support the integration of earlier robotic training in surgical education curricula.

makaleler.baslik: Teaching Informed Consent in Surgical Training: A Scoping Review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Cerrahi Eğitimde Bilgilendirilmiş Onam Eğitimi: Kapsamlı Derleme
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Yapılan kapsamlı derlemede 4337 benzersiz çalışmadan 16'sı dahil edilme kriterlerini karşıladı ve cerrahi eğitimde onam verme öğretiminin, değerlendirmesinin ve ölçütünün büyük ölçüde değişiklik gösterdiği saptandı. Çalışma, pedagojik standartların tanımlanması gerektiğini vurgulamaktadır.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: There is no widely adopted, standardized approach for teaching surgical trainees how to obtain informed consent. Further, no broadly accepted standards exist to characterize the content of methods by which surgical trainees should be taught about conducting informed consent discussions. This scoping review aims to characterize and describe the currently available educational curricula designed to teach informed consent communication to surgical trainees, including medical students on surgery clerkships and surgery residents.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A comprehensive search of 6 databases was performed on January 16, 2025 for relevant studies: MEDLINE, Embase, ERIC, Education Source, Web of Science Core Collection, and MedEdPortal. Studies describing educational interventions to teach U.S. undergraduate medical education (UME) and graduate medical education (GME) trainees surgical informed consent were included in this review. Editorials and opinion pieces, studies conducted outside of the U.S., and those focused on continuing medical education (CME) learners were excluded. This review followed the Arksey and O'Malley scoping review framework and was reported using the PRISMA-ScR guidelines.
RESULTS: The database search yielded 4337 unique studies of which 16 met criteria for inclusion. GME trainees were the focus of interest for most studies. A wide range of teaching methods were implemented by a variety of instructors, including attending surgeons, risk management personnel, and peer educators. 56% of studies (n = 9) reported an informed consent definition including elements of informed consent discussions they taught to trainees. 44% of studies used validated assessment tools (n = 7) to assess interventional impact and there was no overlap of assessment tool utilization between studies.
CONCLUSIONS: This scoping review highlights wide variation in how informed consent is taught, assessed, and evaluated across surgical training. Future efforts should define pedagogical standards for teaching informed consent principles to surgical trainees so that they learn to communicate information in ways patients can understand.

makaleler.baslik: What Should We Write on End of Rotation Evaluations? A Mixed-methods Exploration of General Surgery Resident and Faculty Perspectives.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Rotasyon Sonu Değerlendirmeleri: Asistan ve Eğitici Perspektifleri
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Tek merkezli bu karma yöntemli çalışmada, 9 eğitici ve 8 asistanla yapılan görüşmeler ve 22'şer katılımcıyla yapılan anketler sonucunda, rotasyon sonu değerlendirmelerinin önemsendiği ancak çoğunlukla (%86 asistan, %78 eğitici) düşük kaliteli bulunduğu gösterilmiştir. Katılımcıların %95'i iyileştirme önerilerinin yetersiz olduğunu belirtmiştir (p=0,02).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Narrative comments on resident end-of-rotation (EOR) evaluations are essential to competency-based assessment in surgical training, yet residents often perceive them as poor quality and variably useful. We explored resident and faculty perspectives on satisfaction with EOR comments, what constitutes high-quality comments and barriers to producing them.
METHODS: This is a sequential mixed-methods study at a single academic general surgery residency. Semi-structured interviews with residents and faculty were thematically analyzed using directed content analysis guided by the Relationships, Autonomy, Mastery, and Purpose (RAMP) framework. Findings informed development of resident and faculty surveys assessing perceived purpose, content, barriers, and satisfaction; responses were summarized using medians and interquartile ranges, and dichotomized Likert-scale responses were compared between residents and faculty using chi-square tests.
RESULTS: Of 9 faculty and 8 residents completed interviews, identifying high-quality comments as specific, actionable, balanced, individualized, behaviorally anchored, timely, and purpose-driven. Faculty described relational risk and perceived repercussions as drivers of self-censorship (relationships and autonomy); residents emphasized limited autonomy due to delayed, 1-way feedback (autonomy). Both groups reported feedback quality was often poor (mastery) and did not have a consensus of the goal of EOR comments (purpose). Of 22 residents and 22 faculty (39% response rate each) completed surveys. Most residents and faculty agreed EOR comments are important for resident growth (73% and 68%) and progress (73% and 63%). However, most (86% residents; 78% faculty) reported receiving/writing high-quality comments half the time or less. 95% of residents reported suggestions for improvement were present half the time or less, while 33% of faculty reported including suggestions most of the time/always (p = 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Although both residents and faculty value EOR narrative comments, there is a gap between desired and actual comments. A motivation-informed (RAMP) framework highlights relational and autonomy constraints that may limit candor and actionability.

makaleler.baslik: A Scalable Model for Global Procedural Skills Training: Introduction to SELF.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Küresel Prosedürel Beceri Eğitimi İçin Ölçeklenebilir Bir Model: SELF
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Kaynak kısıtlı ortamlarda prosedürel beceri eğitimini hızlandırmak amacıyla düzenlenen 3 günlük sempozyumda modifiye nominal grup tekniği kullanılmıştır. Uzlaşma çıktısı olarak simülatör tasarımı, öz değerlendirme ve küresel ölçeklendirme stratejileri belirlenmiş ve yeni bir alternatif model önerilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Around the world, demand for surgical care is growing rapidly as populations expand and incomes rise. Procedural skills are still largely taught through apprenticeship models that depend on the availability of experienced instructors and specialized training environments. These constraints make it difficult to scale training fast enough to meet patient needs, particularly in resource-constrained settings. The Surgical Education Learners Forum (SELF) is a global community of practice bringing together clinicians, educators, technologists, and institutions to explore a different model for skills training-one that allows clinicians to learn, practice, and evaluate procedural skills independently. This introductory article of the SELF series introduces the SELF community of practice, the 2023 SELF Symposium, the methodology used at this Symposium to converge on shared recommendations, and the series of articles that follows.
METHODS: In August 2023, SELF convened a global group of medical, educational, and technology leaders for a 3-day symposium in Sunnyvale, California, USA. These leaders sought to reach agreement on the fundamental components of the SELF framework through a series of ideation and convergence exercises, using a semi-anonymized, modified nominal group technique.
RESULTS: The consensus output is presented in the four subsequent articles, which address in sequence: prioritization of procedures for training development, best practices for simulator design in resource-constrained settings, self-administered skills assessment, and strategies for scaling SELF training globally.
CONCLUSIONS: The SELF series of articles charts a route from the long-established maxim of "see one, do one, teach one" toward a scalable alternative for a world that cannot train fast enough by the old model: "see one, teach yourself one, do one."

makaleler.baslik: Assessment of Educational Components of a Short-Term Surgical Trip Partnership: Feasibility and Preliminary Outcomes.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kısa Süreli Cerrahi Eğitim Ortaklığının Değerlendirilmesi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Etiyopya'daki tek merkezde 12 otolarengoloji asistanı ile yapılan prospektif çalışmada, 4 haftalık müfredat sonrasında asistanların naylon (p=0,048), prolene, monocryl ve PDS (p<0,01) kullanımında güvenlerinin arttığı saptanmıştır. 9 ay sonraki takiplerde değerlendirme skorlarında anlamlı değişiklik olmamıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: Assess a longitudinal, education-centered short-term surgical trip partnership's impact on knowledge, technical skill, and learner attitudes among otolaryngology residents.
STUDY DESIGN: Prospective, pre-post interventional study.
SETTING: Single institution in Mekele, Ethiopia.
METHODS: In May 2024, 12 otolaryngology residents participated in a 4-week curriculum of didactics and skills sessions on suture and parotidectomy techniques at Ayder Comprehensive Specialized Hospital. The visiting surgical team administered precurriculum and postcurriculum self-assessments of confidence rated on Likert scales, multiple choice exams (MCE), and Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCE). To assess long-term retention of knowledge and skills, the assessments were also administered 9 months after the initial STST. T-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used to compare precurriculum and postcurriculum outcomes.
RESULTS: The study cohort included 3 PGY1, 4 PGY2, and 5 PGY3 who engaged in an average of 2 parotidectomies, 18 hours of study, and 3 hours of skills practice. Participants had significantly greater postcurriculum confidence in using nylon (P = .048), prolene (P < .01), monocryl (P < .01), and PDS (P < .01) and performing drain stitches (P = .035) and parotidectomy (P = .046) at the end of the first STST. After 9 months, there were no significant changes in assessment scores. All participants reported improved suture skills and strongly agreed that the curriculum was manageable along with clinical tasks.
CONCLUSION: This study provides a framework for building sustainable partnerships across institutions. The education and assessment formats were feasible and improved subjective and objective knowledge and clinical skills. Continued longitudinal tracking of outcomes and their application towards guiding STST partnerships are warranted.

makaleler.baslik: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Periferik Arter Hastalığında Yapay Zekâ ve Amputasyon
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Periferik arter hastalığında amputasyon ve ilgili sonuçları öngören machine learning modellerini değerlendiren ilk meta-analizde 10 çalışma incelendi. Amputasyonla ilgili sonuçlar için havuzlanmış AUC 0,88 (%95 CI, 0,83-0,94) bulundu; kayda dayalı çalışmalar kayda dayalı olmayanlara göre daha yüksek AUC gösterdi (0,92'ye karşı 0,80; p=0,004).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction.
OBJECTIVE: To conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluating the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD.
METHODS: Following PRISMA/PRISMA-S guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and PROBAST risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary ROC (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with GRADE.
RESULTS: Ten studies were included. The pooled AUC for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.855 and specificity 0.836. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than non-registry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; p = 0.004). All models had high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low.
CONCLUSIONS: ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to AI reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

makaleler.baslik: Artificial intelligence in perioperative pressure injury management: a scoping review of evidence, gaps, and implications for population health and digital public health policy.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Perioperatif Basınç Yaralanması Yönetiminde Yapay Zekâ
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Perioperatif basınç yaralanması yönetiminde AI uygulamalarını inceleyen scoping review çalışmasında 6 çalışma dahil edilmiştir. Random Forest ve XGBoost gibi machine learning modelleri kullanılan risk stratifikasyon çalışmalarında en iyi modellerin AUC değerleri 0,806 ile 0,836 arasında bulunmuş, bir çalışma ise 0,9733 tahmin doğruluğu bildirmiştir. Kanıtlar post-hoc risk stratifikasyonunda yoğunlaşmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative pressure injury (POPI) is a significant global public health challenge, contributing to substantial iatrogenic morbidity and heavy economic burden worldwide. Traditional prevention is limited by insufficient assessment tools, the "black box" nature of intraoperative monitoring, and delayed intervention. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a novel approach by integrating multidimensional data for real-time risk prediction; however, no scoping review has systematically mapped AI applications across the full perioperative continuum from a population health perspective.
METHODS: Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to December 11, 2025. Studies applying machine learning, conventional regression-based benchmarking tools, or intelligent sensor-based monitoring for POPI prediction, monitoring, or prevention during the perioperative period were included. Two reviewers independently performed screening and data extraction, followed by descriptive synthesis and evidence mapping.
RESULTS: Six studies (2018-2025), all from East Asia, were included. This geographic concentration highlights an unassessed generalizability and algorithmic fairness risk, rather than an established inequity finding. Evidence concentrated on post-hoc risk stratification (five prediction studies), predominantly using machine learning models (e.g., Random Forest, XGBoost) with AUCs of the best-performing models ranging from 0.806 to 0.836; one study reported a prediction accuracy of 0.9733, which is not directly comparable to AUC. Models identified specialty-specific risk factors (e.g., cardiopulmonary bypass time, forced positioning). Only one proof-of-concept study addressed intraoperative real-time monitoring, visualizing pressure increases after 2 hours of surgery. Evidence for postoperative early warning systems is absent.
CONCLUSION: Current studies demonstrate the feasibility of specialty-specific post-hoc risk stratification using intraoperative covariates, though truly preoperative models remain absent. Intraoperative monitoring shows early promise, but postoperative early warning is a critical gap, and evidence lacks global diversity. Future research should develop closed-loop intelligent systems integrating preoperative prediction, intraoperative multimodal monitoring, and postoperative warning. Nursing protocols should consider incorporating AI-identified risk factors as hypothesis-generating inputs pending prospective validation, while policymakers should establish frameworks for continuous validation and cross-population calibration to ensure equitable impact.

makaleler.baslik: Validation of a Deep Learning Model for Automated Ureteral Length Measurement on CT Against Gross Specimens.
makaleler.baslik_tr: BT Üzerinde Otomatik Üreter Uzunluğu Ölçüm Modeli
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Bu çalışmada 1502 hastadan alınan 3629 BT serisi ile eğitilen derin öğrenme modeli, 70 hastalık prospektif grupta test edilmiştir. Model ile cerrahi örnek ölçümleri arasında anlamlı fark saptanmamıştır (p>0,999).
makaleler.ozet: This study validates a deep learning model for automated ureteral length measurement on CT using gross specimen measurements as the reference standard. A deep learning model was trained on 3629 CT series from 1502 patients (cohort 1) to segment the ureter and extract centerline length. An independent prospective cohort (cohort 2) of 70 patients undergoing radical nephroureterectomy served as the hold-out test set. Each gross specimen was measured twice by one urologist (D1_length and D2_length), with their mean as the reference length (Ref_length). Model-predicted lengths (AI_length) were compared with Ref_length using repeated-measures one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc tests. Determinants of discrepancy were assessed with Spearman correlation and multiple linear regression. Marginal means (± SE) were 266 ± 3.85 mm (D1_length), 273 ± 3.25 mm (D2_length), 269 ± 2.75 mm (AI_length), and 269 ± 3.45 mm (Ref_length). Measurement method had a statistically significant but negligible effect on length (F(3, 207) = 2.73, p = 0.045, η2G = 0.007). D1_length and D2_length differed significantly from Ref_length (both p = 0.002), whereas AI_length was not statistically different from Ref_length (p > 0.999). In regression analysis, reference ureteral length was the only independently associated variable (coefficient - 0.54 mm per mm of reference length, 95% CI - 0.70 to - 0.39; p < 0.001); age, sex, body height, body weight, operation side, and lesion location were not significantly associated. The proposed deep learning pipeline achieved accurate fully automated ureteral segmentation and length measurement across diverse CT acquisition phases and demonstrated close agreement with surgical gross specimen measurements in a prospective clinical cohort, supporting its potential to assist preoperative planning and reduce reliance on manual measurement. The measurement discrepancy was governed primarily by ureteral length itself-with a small systematic underestimation in longer ureters-rather than by patient or procedural factors. However, this tendency, together with the single-center design, and the modest size of the prospective cohort, warrants further multicenter validation before routine clinical deployment.

makaleler.baslik: Ambient Artificial Intelligent Scribes in Oncology: Impact on Clinician Experience and Documentation Burden.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Onkolojide Ortam Yapay Zekâ Sekreterleri
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 958 klinisyenden 190'ının katıldığı çalışmada ambient AI scribe kullanımı değerlendirilmiştir. Adopterler arasında notları kapatma olasılığı değişmezken, not yazma süresinde azalma bildirilmiş (%78'e karşı %60; P=0,043) ve katılımcıların %73'ü aracı önermiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
PURPOSE: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes, widely implemented to reduce clinician burden and dissatisfaction, are not optimized for oncology. We evaluated this technology at-scale at a high-volume cancer center.
METHODS: This prospective mixed-methods study used surveys, electronic health record (EHR), and utilization data to assess adoption, burden, and satisfaction with an ambient AI scribe that was implemented from June to September 2025. Descriptive statistics categorized clinicians as adopters (3+ weeks of use), attempted adopters (1-2 weeks), and never-users (0 weeks). Generalized estimating equations assessed the adoption's effect on the likelihood of closing notes on visit days and pajama time. Pre- and postimplementation surveys obtained clinicians' insights into satisfaction and documentation burden.
RESULTS: In all, 190 (19.8%) of 958 clinicians used the tool, most often with new, video, and in-person visits. Adopters (n = 124) and attempted adopters (n = 66) were more commonly physicians from medicine and surgery. Pre- to post-rollout, the likelihood of closing notes on visit days remained unchanged among never-users (70% v 70%) and decreased among attempted adopters (73% v 70%) and adopters (56% v 54%). Pajama time remained unchanged among attempted adopters (50.6 v 50.1 minutes per week) and decreased among never-users (69.5 v 62.2) and adopters (86.9 v 81.4). Clinicians completing both pre- and postrollout surveys (n = 45) showed a decrease in high/excessive note-writing time (78% v 60%; P = .043). Postrollout surveys (n = 77) showed largely positive experiences, with 73% reporting they would recommend the tool to colleagues.
CONCLUSION: This study of an ambient AI scribe at-scale showed positive satisfaction but mixed burden outcomes among oncology clinicians. Notably, despite enterprise-wide implementation and training, adoption was low and varied by clinician and visit characteristics. Future research should explore adoption barriers and tool optimization to support oncology documentation workflows.

makaleler.baslik: Proprietary platform artificial intelligence-based segmentation of surgical videos facilitates review and rating of operative recordings.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Cerrahi Videolarda Yapay Zekâ Tabanlı Segmentasyon
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Karaciğer grefti hazırlığına ait operatif kayıtların AI tabanlı otomatik segmentasyonunu test eden çalışmada, yapay zekâ video incelemesini ham videoya göre 16 kat, manuel segmentasyona göre ise 96 kat daha hızlı hale getirdi. AI otomatik segmentasyonu ortalama 19,5 adımı yakalarken ortalama teknik not 2,14 ± 0,99 oldu.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in surgery may revolutionize assessment of operative techniques through video capture, auto-segmentation and auto-analysis. The aim of this study was to utilize recordings of a highly standardized surgical intervention, testing the ability of commercially available AI software to auto-segment operative footage in a clinically meaningful way.
METHODS: Twenty-five critical steps in liver graft back-table preparations for connection to a commercially available normothermic perfusion liver pump were determined. Five operative videos were captured manually edited. In addition, using the AI-based GoPro auto-edit feature, the last two recordings were auto-segmented for separate analysis and comparison against the manually edited footage. Each manual and auto-segmented video was assessed for: a) inclusion of each one of the 25 steps, (b) technical performance and completion. The assessment was conducted by an independent experienced transplant surgeon using a modified Likert scale (0-not captured, 1-poor, 2-average, 3-excellent).
RESULTS: Reviewing and rating AI auto-segmented videos was 16 times faster compared to raw video review. Reviewing and rating AI auto-segmented videos was 96 times faster compared to manually segmented recordings, accounting for time needed to edit raw videos. The average number of steps captured between both raw videos and the manually edited videos was 22.5. The average number of steps captured across the AI auto-segmented videos was 19.5 (87%). The average technical grade for the raw and the manually edited videos was 2.58 ± 0.71, and 2.14 ± 0.99 for the AI auto-segmented videos, denoting a rating congruency of 82.9%.
CONCLUSION: AI-based auto-segmentation is an attractive tool for assessment of surgical performance, as it significantly expedites the editing process to prepare footage for review by subject matter experts. To which extent this approach will be applicable outside highly standardized surgical interventions must be further studied.

tez.baslik: Meme kanseri hastalarında yapay zekâ destekli karar sistemlerinin sonuçlarının multidisipliner meme kanseri konsey kararları ile karşılaştırılması
tez.baslik_tr: Meme Kanserinde Yapay Zekâ ve Multidisipliner Konsey Kararları
tez.kisa_ozet: 150 postoperatif meme kanseri olgusunda MDK kararları ile 4 farklı yapay zekâ aracının uyumu karşılaştırılmıştır. Endokrin tedavide doğruluk Singapur YZ'de %96,575, ikincil cerrahide tüm araçlarda %98,667 bulunurken, genetik test önerilerinde uyum zayıf seyretmiştir.
tez.ozet: Amaç: Bu çalışmada, postoperatif meme kanseri olgularında Multidisipliner Meme Konseyi (MDK) kararları ile dört farklı yapay zekâ (YZ) tabanlı klinik karar destek aracının Chatgpt-5.0, Gemini, Openevidence ve Singapur YZ önerileri arasındaki uyum ve performansın, karar başlıklarına göre karşılaştırmalı olarak değerlendirilmesi amaçlandı. Gereç ve Yöntem: Retrospektif tasarımla oluşturulan 150 olguluk postoperatif meme kanseri hastalarından oluşan veri setinde MDK kararları referans standart kabul edildi. Her olgu için yapılandırılmış klinik ve patolojik veriler kullanılarak anonimleştirilmiş biçimde dört yapay zekâ aracına Chatgpt-5.0, Gemini, Openevidence ve Singapur YZ standart bir prompt ile sorgu yapıldı. YZ araçlarından; adjuvan kemoterapi, adjuvan radyoterapi, endokrin tedavi, hedefe yönelik tedavi, ikincil cerrahi, Oncotype önerisi ve genetik test önerisi başlıklarında kararlar alındı. Programların MDK ile uyumu, kendi aralarında uyumu ve uyumsuzluğu arttıran faktörler incelendi. Sistemlerin doğruluk, duyarlılık, özgüllük, PPV/NPV ve F1-skoru ile; uyum ise Cohen's kappa ve Gwet's AC1 ile değerlendirildi; ayrıca marjinal farklılıklar McNemar testi ile incelendi. Bulgular: Karar başlıkları arasında belirgin performans heterojenitesi izlendi. Endokrin tedavide tüm araçların doğruluğu yüksek olup en yüksek değer Singapur YZ'de saptandı (%96,575). Adjuvan radyoterapide en yüksek doğruluk yine Singapur YZ'de (%94,074) ve onu Openevidence izledi (%89,041); bu iki araçta uyum düzeyi daha güçlüydü. Hedefe yönelik tedavi kararlarında en yüksek doğruluk ve uyum Openevidence'ta bulundu (doğruluk %93,197; kappa 0,8195) ve bu başlıkta Openevidence ile MDK arasında yönlü fark saptanmadı. Adjuvan kemoterapi kararlarında doğruluklar orta düzeyde seyretti (en yüksek Gemini %65,753; Openevidence %65,493) ve uyum değerleri genel olarak düşüktü. Oncotype önerisinde doğruluk orta düzeyde olup en yüksek Singapur YZ'de (%78,912) gözlendi. Genetik test önerisinde doğruluklar değişken olmakla birlikte uyum ölçütleri zayıf/negatif seyrederek araçlar arası ve MDK ile tutarlılığın sınırlı olabileceğini düşündürdü. İkincil cerrahi kararlarında tüm araçların doğruluğu çok yüksekti (%98,667). Sonuç: YZ tabanlı karar destek araçlarının MDK süreçlerinde performansı karar başlığına göre belirgin biçimde değişmektedir. Endokrin tedavi, cerrahi tedavi ve radyoterapi gibi kılavuzlarla daha doğrudan eşlenebilen alanlarda doğruluk/uyum oranları daha yüksek iken, adjuvan kemoterapi, Oncotype önerisi ve özellikle genetik test önerisi gibi çok değişkenli klinik bağlam ve eşik yorumlaması gerektiren alanlarda uyum düşebilmektedir. YZ'nin sağlıkta hızla popülerleşmesi ve iş akışlarına entegrasyonu; zaman kazancı, iş yükünün azaltılması, hız ve standardizasyon gibi önemli kazanımlar sağlayabilir. Bununla birlikte, eksik girdi verisine duyarlılık, bağlamı kaçırma, eşik kararlarında tutarsızlık, açıklanabilirlik ve izlenebilirlik kısıtlılığı, güncellik, yerel uygulama uyumsuzluğu ve potansiyel hatalı ve uydurma çıktı riski gibi sınırlılıklar nedeniyle bu araçların klinik kararı ikame edecek şekilde değil, klinisyen gözetiminde ve doğrulama temelli bir yardımcı araç olarak konumlandırılması gereklidir.

makaleler.baslik: Impact of early excision in acute burns: A randomized controlled trial from a tertiary centre in North India.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Akut Yanıklarda Erken Eksizyonun Etkisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 36 hastanın katıldığı RCT'de, akut yanıklarda erken eksizyon median hastane kalış süresini 13,5 güne düşürürken, gecikmiş grupta 28,5 gün bulundu (p=0,009). Polimikrobiyal enfeksiyonlar erken eksizyon grubunda %5,6, gecikmiş grupta %44,4 oranında görüldü (p=0,017).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Early excision and grafting is widely practiced in high-income countries for deep burns; however, its benefit and feasibility in resource-limited settings remain debated. Evidence from randomized studies in low- and middle-income countries is limited.
OBJECTIVE: To compare early versus delayed excision and grafting in acute burn patients in terms of hospital stay, organ dysfunction, wound microbiology, graft take, and transfusion requirements.
METHODS: This prospective, parallel-group, superiority randomized controlled trial with a 1:1 allocation ratio was conducted in the Department of Burns and Plastic Surgery at a tertiary care teaching hospital in North India from April 2024 to September 2025, comparing early versus delayed excision and grafting in acute burn patients, with follow-up completed during the same admission period. Adults aged 18-60 years with 10-40% total body surface area (TBSA) deep second- or third-degree burns were randomized into early excision (≤7 days post-burn) or delayed excision groups. The primary outcome was length of hospital stay. Secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on day 10, wound microbiology, graft take on postoperative day 7 and transfusion requirements. Continuous variables were analysed using the Mann-Whitney U test and categorical variables using Fisher's exact test.
RESULTS: Thirty-six patients were randomized (18 early excision, 18 delayed excision). Early excision significantly reduced median hospital stay (13.5 vs 28.5 days, p = 0.009). The median time from burn injury to excision was 4.5 days (IQR: 3-6 days) in the early excision group and 30.5 days (IQR: 23.5-42.5 days) in the delayed excision group. No significant differences were observed in SOFA score, blood transfusion requirements, or mortality. There was no statistically significant difference in overall burn wound culture positivity between groups (p = 0.092). However, polymicrobial infections occurred significantly more frequently in the delayed excision group (44.4% vs 5.6%, p = 0.017). Graft take during the index admission was lower in the early excision group.
CONCLUSION: Early excision significantly reduced hospital stay and was associated with fewer polymicrobial wound infections without increasing organ dysfunction or transfusion requirements. Larger multicentre randomized studies are warranted to confirm these findings and further evaluate graft-related outcomes.

makaleler.baslik: Prophylactic Negative Pressure Wound Therapy Versus Standard Wound Care Among Lower Extremity Amputations: A Meta-Analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Alt Ekstremite Amputasyonunda Profilaktik NPWT
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 893 hastanın dahil olduğu meta-analizde, profilaktik kapalı insizyon NPWT, standart yara bakımına kıyasla daha düşük postoperatif SSI (OR 0,370; p=0,044) ve yara dehisansı (OR 0,224; p=0,008) oranları ile ilişkilendirilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet: Prophylactic closed incisional negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce postoperative wound complications following lower extremity amputation in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD). We conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate whether closed incisional NPWT reduces wound complications compared with standard wound care (SWC) in this high-risk vasculopathic population. A systematic search was performed to identify studies comparing closed incisional NPWT and SWC among patients with PAD undergoing lower extremity amputation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 2025 using predefined search strings. Six studies met eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models as the primary analysis to account for anticipated clinical and methodological heterogeneity across studies. Leave-one-out analyses and an analysis excluding the study in which NPWT was delivered as part of a multifaceted care bundle were performed to assess robustness. A total of 893 patients were included, including 408 in the closed incisional NPWT group and 485 in the SWC group. Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative surgical site infection (SSI) (OR = 0.370; 95% CI = 0.143-0.957; P = .044) and wound dehiscence (OR = 0.224; 95% CI = 0.125-0.401; P = .008). Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative SSI and wound dehiscence following lower extremity amputation in patients with PAD. Because the evidence is predominantly observational and prediction intervals included the null value, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in adequately powered randomized trials.

makaleler.baslik: Healthcare-associated infections in Singapore's long-term acute care hospitals: results from the first national point prevalence survey.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Singapur Uzun Süreli Akut Bakım Hastanelerinde Sağlıkla İlişkili Enfeksiyonlar
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Singapur'daki 9 uzun süreli akut bakım hastanesinde yürütülen ilk ulusal nokta prevalans anketidir. 1.546 hasta arasında 86 kişide 94 enfeksiyon saptanmış olup prevalans %5,6 (%95 CI 4,5-6,8) bulunmuştur. En sık görülen enfeksiyonlar sepsis (%36,2), idrar yolu enfeksiyonu (%24,5) ve cerrahi alan enfeksiyonudur (%18,1).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: While healthcare-associated infection (HAI) surveillance in Singapore's acute care hospitals is well established, comparable data from long-term acute care hospitals (LTACHs), known as community hospitals, are limited. We conducted the first national point prevalence survey (PPS) to determine HAI prevalence in Singapore LTACHs.
METHODS: A standardized protocol adapted from the Singapore acute care hospital HAI PPS protocol, which was adapted from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control protocol for acute care hospitals, was implemented across 9 LTACHs. Adult inpatients present in participating wards at 8 a.m. on the survey day were included. Data on patient characteristics, invasive devices, and active infections were collected from electronic medical records. Factors associated with HAIs were determined using multivariate logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 1,546 patients, 86 had 94 HAIs, corresponding to a prevalence of 5.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.5-6.8). The most common infection types were unspecified sepsis (36.2%), urinary tract infection (UTI) (24.5%), and surgical site infection (18.1%). Microbiological confirmation was available for 25.5% of HAIs, with Enterobacterales (54.8%) most frequently identified. Presence of central vascular catheter (odds ratio [OR]: 3.88; 95% CI: 1.66-9.08) and peripheral vascular catheter (OR: 10.48; 95% CI: 6.45-17.03) were associated with HAIs, while larger hospital size (≥250 beds) was associated with reduced odds (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-0.99).
CONCLUSION: This inaugural PPS establishes the baseline for HAIs in Singapore's LTACHs. Findings suggest broad infection prevention initiatives may provide the greatest benefit sector-wide, while the high UTI burden highlights an opportunity for targeted prevention strategies.

makaleler.baslik: Intelligent thermoregulation strategy versus routine thermal management on myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery during gastrointestinal tumor resection in elderly patients (SAGE): a multicenter, parallel-group, superiority trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: GİS Tümör Cerrahisinde Akıllı Termoregülasyon
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Yaşlı hastalarda GİS tümör rezeksiyonu sırasında uygulanan akıllı termoregülasyon stratejisinin miyokardiyal hasar üzerindeki etkisini değerlendiren çok merkezli bir RCT'dir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Inadvertent perioperative hypothermia is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but adequately powered trials using high-sensitivity troponin endpoints is lacking. The SAGE trial evaluates whether an intelligent, closed-loop thermoregulation strategy reduces myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS) in high-risk elderly patients.
METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, parallel-group, randomized controlled superiority trial conducted at seven tertiary hospitals in China. Participants aged ≥65 years scheduled for elective gastrointestinal tumor resection under general anesthesia are randomly assigned (1:1) to intelligent closed-loop warming (target 36.8 °C, upper limit 37.0 °C) or routine thermal management (active warming only if core temperature ≤35.5 °C). The primary outcome is the incidence of MINS within the first 2 postoperative days , adjudicated using high-sensitivity troponin thresholds per AHA criteria. Secondary outcomes include surgical site infection, transfusion requirement, hypothermia burden, emergence delirium, delayed emergence, and postoperative shivering. With 695 participants per group (total 1,390, accounting for 10% dropout), the trial has 80% power at a one-sided significance level of 0.05 to detect a 6 absolute percentage point reduction in MINS (12% to 6%) with a superiority margin of -2 percentage points.
DISCUSSION: The SAGE trial is designed to generate new evidence on the relationship between intraoperative hypothermia exposure and postoperative cardiovascular complications. It will evaluate whether closed-loop targeted normothermia reduces myocardial injury and will explore hypothermia exposure thresholds that may inform individualized perioperative management for geriatric surgical patients.
TRIAL ACRONYM: Intelligent Thermoregulation Strategy for Advanced-Age Elders undergoing gastrointestinal tumor resection (SAGE).
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR), identifier: ChiCTR2600117264. Registered on January 21, 2026 (http://www.chictr.org.cn).

makaleler.baslik: Timing of First Systemic Antibiotic Administration and Risk of Deep Infection in Adults with Open Long-Bone Fractures: A Systematic Review and Threshold-Specific Evidence Synthesis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Açık Uzun Kemik Kırıklarında İlk Antibiyotik Zamanlaması ve Derin Enfeksiyon Riski
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Açık kırığı olan yetişkinlerde ilk sistemik antibiyotik uygulaması zamanlaması incelenmiştir. 191 hastadan oluşan bir kohortta, acil servis varışından 60 dakika sonra düzeltilmiş odds oranı 1,02 (%95 CI 0,39-2,68) olarak bildirilmiştir. Gözlemsel ilişkiler nedensel eşikler oluşturmamaktadır.
makaleler.ozet: Background/Objectives: Early systemic antibiotics are central to open-fracture care, but a 60 min operational target does not establish a biological infection threshold. We examined how time origin, cutoff, and outcome definition affect interpretation of reported associations. Methods: Evidence was reconstructed from two preserved bibliographic inventories containing 24 entries. Complete database-search exports were unavailable, and selection, extraction, ROBINS-E, and GRADE were not independently duplicated. The protocol was archived retrospectively on OSF (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/7J8QN). Estimates were described separately by time origin, cutoff, adjustment, outcome, and follow-up for a target population aged at least 18 years. No pooled estimate was retained. Results: The historical evidence map contained 16 reports, including contextual reports that did not establish applicability to the target population. This is not a verified final included-study count. Within the preserved inventory, no threshold-by-time-origin group supplied two compatible adjusted estimates. A 191-patient cohort reported an adjusted odds ratio of 1.02 (95% CI 0.39-2.68) at 60 min after emergency-department arrival. Recorded appraisals indicated predominantly high or very high risk of bias and very low certainty; these judgements were not independently verified. Conclusions: Distinguishing care-process targets from causal thresholds improves interpretation of the available reports. However, incomplete searching and single-investigator assessment limit the reliability and completeness of this synthesis. The observational associations establish neither causal thresholds nor the safety of delay and do not justify postponing indicated prophylaxis.

gundem.baslik: Randomized Trial of Hypofractionated Postmastectomy Radiation Therapy in Women With Breast Reconstruction (RT CHARM, Alliance A221505).
gundem.baslik_tr: Meme Rekonstrüksiyonu Sonrası Hipofraksiyone PMRT: Randomize Çalışma
gundem.kisa_ozet: Meme rekonstrüksiyonu yapılan 898 hastayı içeren RCT'de, 3,9 yıllık medyan takip sonucunda 24 aylık rekonstrüksiyon komplikasyon oranları hipofraksiyone PMRT kolunda %12,3, konvansiyonel PMRT kolunda %10,2 bulundu (tahmini fark -%2,1; %95 CI, -6,5 ila 2,2). 36 aylık lokorejyonel nüks oranlarında istatistiksel olarak anlamlı fark saptanmadı (%1,5'e karşı %2,2). Hipofraksiyone PMRT, rekonstrüksiyon uygulanan kadınlarda güvenli ve noninferior bulunmuştur.
gundem.ozet:
PURPOSE: Patients with breast cancer requiring postmastectomy radiation therapy (PMRT) often desire breast reconstruction. Reconstructions can be adversely affected by PMRT, and fear of reconstruction complications has discouraged adoption of short-course radiation therapy used after lumpectomy. To fill the evidence gap, we conducted a noninferiority trial of hypofractionated versus conventional PMRT in patients undergoing breast reconstruction. The primary outcome was reconstruction complication rate, a composite of wound healing, readmission, capsular contracture, unplanned reoperation, and reconstruction failure.
METHODS: Women with unilateral invasive breast cancer with planned immediate or delayed reconstruction and PMRT were randomly assigned (1:1) to 50 Gy (25 fractions/5 weeks) or 42.56 Gy (16 fractions/3 weeks). This study was designed with a noninferiority margin of 10%, assuming a 2-year reconstruction complication rate of 25% with conventional PMRT. Randomization was stratified by immediate versus delayed and autologous versus implant-only reconstruction.
RESULTS: Between 2018 and 2021, 898 patients enrolled with a median follow-up of 3.9 years; 825 patients were evaluable for the primary end point. The 24-month reconstruction complication rates were 12.3% (52/422) with hypofractionated PMRT and 10.2% (41/403) with conventional PMRT, corresponding to an estimated difference of -2.1% (95% CI, -6.5 to 2.2). The complication rate was higher (regardless of arm) with implant-only versus autologous reconstruction (odds ratio = 1.65). There was no statistically significant difference in 36-month locoregional recurrence rates: 1.5% (95% CI, 0.7 to 3.2) with hypofractionated and 2.2% (95% CI, 1.1 to 4.3) with conventional PMRT. Acute and late toxicity rates were not statistically different.
CONCLUSION: A 16-fraction course of hypofractionated PMRT is safe and noninferior to conventional PMRT in women undergoing breast reconstruction after mastectomy.
