gundem.baslik: EAES-SAGES clinical practice guideline update: multi-society recommendations on key controversies in the management of diverticular disease.
gundem.baslik_tr: Divertiküler Hastalık Yönetiminde Güncel EAES-SAGES Kılavuzu
gundem.kisa_ozet: Semptomatik komplike olmayan divertiküler hastalık, komplike olmayan ve komplike divertikülit yönetimine ilişkin kanıta dayalı öneriler sunulmuştur. Sistemik derlemede 27 çalışma incelenmiş olup rifaksimin, mesalamin veya antibiyotik kullanımı gibi konularda koşullu öneriler verilmiştir.
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: We identified areas of controversy in the management of patients with diverticular disease to develop key questions addressing the management of symptomatic uncomplicated diverticular disease (SUDD), uncomplicated diverticulitis, and complicated diverticulitis.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review to identify randomized trials and cohort studies addressing our key questions. Informed by an updated evidence synthesis, an international, multidisciplinary panel of gastrointestinal surgeons, gastroenterologists, patient partners, and methodologists applied the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) evidence-to-decision framework during panel consensus meetings to derive recommendations for the management of patients with diverticular disease.
RESULTS: The systematic review identified 27 studies representing very low to moderate certainty evidence. The panel made the following recommendations: 1. In patients with SUDD, we suggest rifaximin or mesalamine over standard supportive care (conditional recommendation); 2. In patients with uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine antibiotics (conditional recommendation); 3. In patients with persistent symptoms following an episode of recurrent uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest elective resection over observation (conditional recommendation); 4. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine follow-up colonoscopy (conditional recommendation); 5. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of diverticulitis complicated by an abscess, we suggest elective resection over surveillance (conditional recommendation). The panel judged that a significant proportion of patients would place a high value in reducing the risk of recurrence at 1 year but also acknowledged the lack of evidence addressing prioritized outcomes including 30-day major complications, need for emergency surgery, stoma-free survival at 1 year, and quality of life at 1 year. Given that patient values and preferences may vary, clinicians are encouraged to apply patient-centered decision-making and discuss the alternatives.
CONCLUSION: This clinical practice guideline update provides evidence-informed recommendations to support patients and clinicians in the management of diverticular disease.

gundem.baslik: Rapid versus slow puncture in endoscopic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy: a multicenter randomized crossover trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: EUS Eşliğinde Karaciğer Biyopsisinde Hızlı ve Yavaş İğne Teknikleri
gundem.kisa_ozet: 62 örneğin analiz edildiği çok merkezli randomize çapraz çalışmada, hızlı delme tekniği geleneksel yavaş delme tekniğine kıyasla portal trakt sayısını (ortalama fark 2,39; %95 CI 1,50-3,27) ve toplam örnek uzunluğunu (ortalama fark 15,19 mm; %95 CI 9,65-20,74) anlamlı derecede artırmıştır.
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy (EUS-LB) is increasingly used for hepatic histologic assessment; however, optimal technical approaches remain undefined. This prospective, multicenter clinical study aimed to compare tissue acquisition and safety between the rapid and slow puncture techniques for EUS-LB.
METHODS: This was a multicenter randomized crossover study. Patients undergoing EUS-LB were randomized to receive both rapid puncture and slow puncture techniques in alternating sequence during the same session. The primary outcomes were the number of complete portal tracts (CPTs) and total specimen length (TSL). The secondary outcomes were diagnostic adequacy and adverse events. Linear mixed models and generalized linear mixed models were used to evaluate the technical performance.
RESULTS: A total of 62 specimens were analyzed. Compared with the conventional slow puncture technique, rapid puncture significantly increased CPTs (mean difference 2.39; 95%CI 1.50-3.27), as well as TSL (mean difference 15.19 mm; 95%CI 9.65-20.74), with corresponding improvements in diagnostic adequacy (odds ratio 16.27, 95%CI 2.41-109.97). Time period and center were not statistically significantly associated with the outcomes. No severe adverse events were reported.
CONCLUSION: The modified rapid puncture technique was associated with improved specimen quality in EUS-LB. These findings support its potential utility in clinical practice; however, further validation in larger and more diverse populations is warranted.

gundem.baslik: Preoperative Injection of Botulinum Toxin Into the Sphincter of Oddi Does Not Prevent Pancreatic Fistula After Distal Pancreatectomy: The Randomized Controlled PREBOTPilot Trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: Distal Pankreatektomi Sonrası Botulinum Toksin Enjeksiyonu Pankreatik Fistülü Önlemiyor
gundem.kisa_ozet: 50 hastanın alındığı monokentli RCT'de, cerrahi öncesi Sphincter of Oddi'ye botulinum toksin enjeksiyonunun distal pancreatectomy sonrası klinik olarak anlamlı POPF oranını azaltmadığı gösterildi (intervention grubunda %28,6, kontrol grubunda %15; p=0.294).
gundem.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether preoperative injection of botulinum toxin (BTX) into the sphincter of Oddi (SO) is a safe and feasible strategy to prevent postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) after distal pancreatectomy (DP).
SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: POPF remains a common and potentially serious complication following DP, affecting up to 30% of patients. Pharmacologically induced sphincter relaxation by endoscopic injection of BTX into the SO has been described as a new approach to prevent POPF after DP by improved drainage of pancreatic fluid towards the duodenum.
METHODS: Patients scheduled for elective primary distal pancreatectomy (DP), irrespective of the underlying disease, were included in this monocenter, randomized controlled, open-label, phase-II trial with 2 parallel arms. Patients randomly assigned to the intervention group received an endoscopic injection of BTX (100 units) into the SO 3-10 days before surgery. Patients in the control group did not undergo any preoperative intervention. The combined primary endpoint was defined as the occurrence of clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF grades B/C) and/or death due to any cause within 30 days following DP.
RESULTS: From March 2020 to August 2023, 50 patients were included in the trial. Subsequent to the analysis of the primary endpoint, which revealed no tendency of a beneficial effect on the rate of POPF after DP following BTX injection, even with the most favorable outcome upon further inclusion of the remaining 10 patients planned for recruitment, the recruitment was prematurely terminated. All 26 patients in the intervention group underwent successful SO BTX injection within a median of 6 (IQR of 5-8) days before surgery. DP was performed in 41 patients (82%). Postinterventional pancreatitis was not detected. Within 30 days, POPF grade B/C occurred in 6 patients in the intervention and 3 patients in the control group (28.6% vs. 15%, P=0.294). One patient in the intervention group died during the trial due to POPF-induced postpancreatectomy hemorrhage (PPH).
CONCLUSION: Preoperative injection of BTX into the SO did not reduce clinically relevant POPF or 30-day mortality following DP, and the trial was prematurely terminated for futility. Although the intervention was safe and feasible, these findings do not support its use for the prevention of POPF after DP.

gundem.baslik: IHPBA 2026 global guideline for the management of hepatocellular carcinoma in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
gundem.baslik_tr: Kaynak Kısıtlı Sağlık Sistemlerinde HCC Yönetimi İçin Global Kılavuz
gundem.kisa_ozet: IHPBA kaynak kısıtlı ortamlarda HCC tanısı ve tedavisi için global bir kılavuz yayınladı. Karaciğer rezeksiyonu korunmuş karaciğer fonksiyonlu tek veya sınırlı lezyonlarda tercih edilirken, sistemik tedavi olarak atezolizumab/bevacizumab kombinasyonu önerildi.
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines for the management of patients with HCC are predominantly focused on well-resourced healthcare systems. In 2024, the IHPBA Legacy committee initiated a process to develop global resource-sensitive guidelines for the management of HCC.
METHODS: An IHPBA global guideline group produced and circulated statements on the management of HCC from diagnosis to treatment, discussed these in online webinars and generated guidelines. This document focuses on the diagnosis and management of patients with HCC in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
RESULTS: Initial diagnosis by ultrasound is supported by cross-sectional imaging. Alfa-feto protein and assessment of liver synthetic function are recommended at diagnosis. Lesion biopsy is not mandated. Liver resection is the recommended treatment of choice for single HCC in patients with preserved liver function and up to 3 lesions ≤3 cm. Radiofrequency and microwave are regarded as equivalent and can be used if resection is not available. Ethanol injection can be used if thermal ablation is not available but should be restricted to small lesions. TACE and TAE can be used for intermediate stage disease. Atezolizumab/bevacizumab combination is recommended as first line systemic therapy with sorafenib and Lenvatinib being recommended if first line is not an option. Advice for the care of the patient with advanced or terminal disease is provided.
CONCLUSIONS: This document provides resource-sensitive HCC guidelines that prioritise feasibility, maximise benefit, and reduce default reliance on best supportive care alone and are produced for the IHPBA by discussion with the global community of IHPBA.
gundem.dergi_tam: HPB : the official journal of the International Hepato Pancreato Biliary Association
